articles.summary: Luka Doncic had five steals and two blocks in the Los Angeles Lakers’ 124-114 win over the Atlanta Hawks on Monday, yet he still wants the team to defend
articles.body: Luka Doncic had five steals and two blocks in the Los Angeles Lakers’ 124-114 win over the Atlanta Hawks on Monday, yet he still wants the team to defend better. He returned after missing Sunday’s game with lower back tightness and finished with 32 points, 10 assists and eight rebounds.Los Angeles has won six straight and sits at 10-2, but Doncic pointed to the one number he did not like. The Lakers entered Monday ranked 21st in defensive efficiency, a spot he believes is well below what the roster can reach.What did Luka Doncic say about the Lakers’ defense?Doncic told reporters the Lakers can climb well past 21st. “I think we have the potential for that,” he said.His own night backed up the point. The Lakers guard did a lot of the damage with his hands, and the team finished with 16 steals, three from Matisse Thybulle and two from Ziaire Williams. Those takeaways turned into 29 points while Austin Reaves (illness) and Quentin Grimes (right finger sprain) sat out. Los Angeles also blocked six shots, two of them by Doncic.Atlanta still found ways to score. The Hawks hit 17 of 44 from 3-point range and grabbed 12 offensive rebounds to the Lakers’ eight, though those boards produced only eight second-chance points, two fewer than Los Angeles got. CJ McCollum and Aaron Wiggins combined for 36 points off Atlanta’s bench. The Lakers gave up 35 points in the second quarter and 33 in the third. They led by as many as 20 and won by 10.At 10-2 with the 21st-ranked defense, the Lakers are winning on offense and takeaways. Doncic is asking the rest of the game to catch up.Doncic’s 45-point week earned Western Conference honorsThe NBA named the guard Western Conference Player of the Week for games played Nov. 2 to 8. It was the fifth time he has won the award with Los Angeles and the 20th in his career. Doncic averaged 45.0 points, 7.0 rebounds and 8.3 assists on 52.5% shooting from the field and 39.5% from 3-point range, and the Lakers won all three games he played.He opened with 42 points and 13 assists in a 138-117 win over Miami, then scored 40 in a 116-103 victory at Sacramento. His season-high 53 came in a 124-118 NBA Cup win over Portland, which put him with Elgin Baylor, George Mikan and Kobe Bryant as the only Lakers to score 40 or more in four straight games.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Joel Embiid injury update: Latest on Sixers star after awkward fall during high-stakes against Celtics
articles.summary: Joel Embiid went down hard in the closing seconds of the first half as the Sixers chased the Celtics on Tuesday night.
articles.body: Joel Embiid went down hard in the closing seconds of the first half as the Sixers chased the Celtics on Tuesday night. The center missed a transition layup, slipped on the landing and rolled over in pain. Embiid got up and ran back on defense, but the limp was easy to see. Boston also led by double digits at the break, and the Sixers need Embiid to find a rhythm after a rough start to his season. Both teams entered as the top two in the East, which made the scare hard to ignore.What happened to Joel Embiid against the Celtics?Boston won the first quarter 30-23 and kept pushing in the second, so Philadelphia was already behind before the fall. Embiid went up for a transition layup and missed. A slip of the right foot on the landing sent the big man crashing, and the planted left foot tweaked the ankle. The quarter ended seconds later, and Embiid limped to the locker room for halftime.The news after the break was better. Embiid returned to start the third quarter and snapped the shooting slump with a three-pointer. Neither moment settles how the ankle feels, and no further word on it had come out at that stage.Asked what felt off after Sunday’s win over the Bulls, Embiid answered with one word, everything, and framed the fix this way: “Figuring out how to just be myself again.”Shooting slump adds to the early concernThe first half was rough even before the fall. Embiid played 17 minutes and missed all six shots from the field, two of them from three. The nine points all came at the line, where Embiid hit nine of 11 attempts. Five rebounds and two turnovers rounded out the half.Sunday against the Bulls was little better from the floor. Embiid went 7-for-19, missed both three-point tries and dropped to 3-for-30 from deep this season. The center did grab 10 rebounds, eight on the offensive glass, but most were cleanups of Embiid’s own misses.Injuries have defined Embiid’s NBA career so far, and the main fear around this Sixers season was a physical issue cutting it short. A fall like this one brings that fear back. A hobbled Embiid would hurt Philadelphia’s chances of coming back in this game and holding its place at the top of the East.Philadelphia has Tyrese Maxey, V.J. Edgecombe, LeBron James, and Jaylen Brown around Embiid, and a 9-2 start shows the team can win while the big man searches for form.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Jayson Tatum responds to Jaylen Brown snub with runaway Celtics win over 76ers paced by Paul George's 36 points
articles.summary: Jaylen Brown delivered the opening message with a pregame snub Tuesday night. But it was Jayson Tatum, Paul George and the Boston Celtics who got the last wo...
articles.body:
Jaylen Brown delivered the opening message with a pregame snub Tuesday night. But it was Jayson Tatum, Paul George and the Boston Celtics who got the last word in a runaway 123-101 win over Brown's Philadelphia 76ers.

The game marked the anticipated first meeting between Tatum and Brown since their highly publicized split as Celtics teammates. The pair led Boston to an NBA championship, but are off to a bitter start as rivals after Brown's offseason trade to the 76ers.

Tatum got the best of Brown in the blowout win with 21 points, 6 rebounds, 4 assists and 2 blocks. Brown got into early foul trouble with three first-half fouls and struggled to get much of anything going. He finished with 13 points, 5 rebounds, 2 assists and 4 turnovers.

In the end, it was George who took on the starring role against his former team. George was part of the return from Philadelphia in the deal to acquire Brown from the Celtics. He caught fire and led all scorers with 36 points and five rebounds while shooting 14 of 22 from the field and 6 of 11 from 3.

The tension was on display from the opening tip as Brown openly snubbed Tatum in front of 20,000-plus fans in Philadelphia and a national TV audience. Brown said prior to Tuesday's highly anticipated 76ers-Celtics game that he didn't intend to speak with Tatum .

As players took the court before tipoff, Tatum approached his former Celtics teammate in an effort to dap Brown up. Brown, who was busy spinning the basketball, acted like Tatum didn't exist.

Tatum then moved on to Brown's teammate, LeBron James, who was happy to share some pregame love with his rival before getting down to the business of basketball.

It was awkward to say the least and left Tatum standing at midcourt next to Brown like a man who'd just been left hanging.

The ball was then mercifully tipped to break the pregame tension. After the game, Brown told reporters he was simply trying to focus rather than snub Tatum, via ESPN's Kris Rhim :

"I'm just focused on coming out and doing what's best for my team. Everything else was just — to be honest, I wasn't paying attention. But credit to Jayson, he played well tonight. Credit to the Celtics, they executed, shot the hell out of the ball. They were the better team tonight."

When the game action started, it was Tatum who struck the first blow. In their first one-on-one matchup of the game, Brown sized Tatum up from the wing beyond the 3-point arc. Tatum smothered him and poked the ball away off Brown and out of bounds for a turnover.

Tatum went on to score 11 first-quarter points as the Celtics finished the frame with a 30-23 lead.

From there Tatum and Brown spent much of the game guarding each other when they shared the court. But Tatum made his biggest mark on the game with a poster dunk on James in the second half as the 76ers were closing the gap from a 13-point third-quarter deficit.

The 76ers did battle back to tie the game at 76. But hot Celtics 3-point shooting paced by George opened the game up down the stretch as Boston opened its lead to as much as 25 points.

The Celtics shot 50.5% from the field and 44.9% (22 of 45) from 3 while holding the 76ers to 41.8% shooting and a 29.7% clip (11 of 37) from 3.

Tyrese Maxey led the 76ers with 24 points. James tallied 11 points, 8 rebounds and 5 assists while shooting 1 of 6 from 3. Joel Embiid had 16 points and 6 rebounds while shooting 2 of 9 from the field.

The end result was a blowout win for the Celtics (9-2) to overtake the 76ers (9-3) for the best record in the Eastern Conference.

No postgame interaction between Tatum, Brown

When it was over, Brown shared hugs with several of his former Celtics teammates. But he walked off the court without acknowledging Tatum as Tatum gave a postgame interview to NBC.

Tatum, meanwhile, didn't say Brown's name in his interview while downplaying the meaning of Tuesday's win.

"They all count as one," Tatum said of the game result. "No game is bigger than the other, definitely in the regular season. It's one game. It's one game. The hoopla is definitely over, and we get ready for tomorrow."

Considering the chatter leading up to Tuesday's game, Brown's cold reception to Tatum was expected.

Tatum has downplayed any friction with his former All-NBA teammate.

"There's no animosity, there's no beef," Tatum said previously when talking about his relationship with Brown.

For Brown, who was vocal about his multitude of grievances before the Celtics traded him in the offseason, there's clearly beef. Or lamb chops, as he prefers.

"There's no beef, but there might be a little lamb chops and gravy," Brown previously opined on his relationship with Tatum.

Brown doubled down on Sunday that he doesn't have anything to talk about with Tatum.

"I mean, he's on his side, I'm on my side," Brown said, per ESPN's Kris Rhim . "Just playing basketball. Both of us are trying to win, so nothing to talk about. Just check the ball up."

Check the ball up, they did — this time in favor of Tatum and the Celtics.

articles.summary: The main storyline ahead of Tuesday's Philadelphia 76ers vs. Boston Celtics matchup was the drama brewing between Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum. Their pregame "greeting" added a few more logs to the fire.
articles.body:
The main storyline ahead of Tuesday's Philadelphia 76ers vs. Boston Celtics matchup was the drama brewing between Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum. Their pregame "greeting" added a few more logs to the fire.

But the Celtics quickly shot that narrative into the background.

Celtics' Shootaround Song Ahead of Tatum vs. Brown 🌶️

Behind Boston's red-hot shooting and some foul trouble from Brown, the Celtics rolled to a 123-101 win over the Sixers in the first matchup between the rivals this season.

Here's a look at the game's key performers:

The Celtics staged a full blitzkrieg from beyond the arc on Tuesday night, finishing 22-of-49 from three. It was a pure expression of Joe Mazzulla ball.

The Sixers struggled from beyond the arc, meanwhile, finishing just 11-of-37 from three. That discrepancy in perimeter shooting played an enormous role in Boston's victory.

And while much of the pregame hype centered on Brown vs. Tatum, it was Paul George who truly had a memorable revenge game, torching his former team.

Tuesday was a case study in how the Celtics (9-2) want to win—spread the floor, hit a bunch of threes, play good defense. It's a difficult formula to deal with when the threes are falling at a high rate.

For the Sixers (9-3), meanwhile, it was a reminder that the halfcourt offense remains a work in progress, though it was also just a poor shooting night. Boston's defense certainly contributed to that, and the barrage of threes gave the Sixers less chances to steal easy buckets in transition, a hallmark of their success to this point.

These teams will play three more times this season, though the next matchup won't be until Jan. 21. Round 1 went to the Celtics in resounding fashion.

articles.title: Jaylen Brown snubbed Jayson Tatum before tipoff. His night against the Celtics only got worse
articles.summary: Jaylen Brown's emotional reunion with Jayson Tatum couldn't have gone much worse. And his struggles against Boston may be a sign of a much bigger problem in...
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA — The final blow to the 76ers' chest — and their ego — came with five minutes remaining in the fourth quarter, as Paul George held his follow-through in front of his former bench and Jayson Tatum stretched his wings toward his teammate in celebration.

In stark contrast, Jaylen Brown's confusion over a busted coverage was plastered all over his face as he and the veteran, star-studded bunch shuffled back to their seats before the white flag was raised. What should have been a hotly contested duel had flamed out rather quickly, with hundreds of fans heading for the exits and a blowout in full effect.

"I'm a bit frustrated, honestly," Brown said following the 123-101 defeat . "I wanted to perform better for my team. Foul trouble kind of derailed me a little bit, but it happens. It's unfortunate but you gotta just move on to the next."

For weeks, the sheer build-up to Tuesday night essentially guaranteed an emotional apex. Cryptic messages, subtle shots and narratives built on both sides of the Tatum-Brown divide dominated headlines, airwaves and basketball discourse. Something was bound to give.

But even in that, Brown's emotions quite possibly got the best of him. Seconds before tipoff, after the tidal wave of boos, tension and apprehension had consumed the building, Brown had a golden opportunity to bury the hatchet as Tatum approached him near midcourt. An embrace, nod or handshake — something to acknowledge the near-decade relationship between the two — was set up perfectly. Instead, Brown chose in that moment to ignore Tatum as he tapped his former teammate's arm and chest twice.

It didn't end there. Brown used every opportunity he had to latch onto Tatum like an All-Pro cornerback, at times not even recognizing the ongoing action around him. When he received the ball, he put his head down and charged at opposing defenders recklessly, unable to generate rhythm — and the rampant roars from the Philly faithful only compounded Brown's downhill desperation and aggression. (Brown recorded his second-highest first-quarter usage rate this season, paired poorly with a 28.6 turnover rate.) A failure to find an offensive groove carried over to the other side of the ball, with Brown giving away cheap fouls, forcing him to sit and ultimately limiting him to just 25 minutes. His final tally told the story better than anything else could: 13 points, four turnovers and a game-worst minus-27.

"I'm just focused on coming out and doing what's best for my team," Brown said. "Everything else was, to be honest, I wasn't paying attention. But credit to Jayson, he played well tonight. Credit to the Celtics, they executed and shot the hell out of the ball. They were the better team tonight."

To add insult to injury, it was Tatum and George who looked like they had played for nine years together instead of the three weeks. Boston has found a way to harmonize the pair's similar skill sets, as both combine usage ( 100th and 91st percentiles , respectively) with creation chops (98th and 87th percentiles). One of George's underrepresented qualities is his ability to assimilate within different ecosystems while not detracting from the order of operations. The Celtics have outscored opponents by 33 points in the 162 minutes both have shared the floor, a promising early sign for the league's No. 2 team in net rating. Both George and Tatum can play off the other, whether it's darting around screens and relocating, spacing the floor or drawing defenses to one side of the floor. The pair accounted for 18 of Boston's 49 attempted 3s, a hand-in-glove fit for Mazzulla ball — in addition to 56 points, 9 treys, 11 rebounds and 5 assists, feasting upon their prey. Beef. Lamb chops. Gravy.

For Brown, the conversation will continue surrounding how the former Finals MVP truly fits within the 76ers' structure. And it's not just that he's converting shots and handling the ball at rates not seen in over seven years , it's that his entire offensive makeup has changed drastically. Last season — the campaign Brown notoriously proclaimed as his favorite of his career — he operated as a lead ball-handler nearly 25 percent of the time on the floor, per Synergy tracking data. That volume has plummeted to just seven percent, with the bulk of his opportunities coming via spot-ups or in transition. Brown is certainly not as fluid or creative a playmaker as his former teammate Tatum or even George, but the sudden removal of opportunities certainly comes with its own trickle-down effects.

"He had a tough night," 76ers head coach Nick Nurse said. "They did a pretty good job of swarming him and sending multiple defenders."

The larger theme, one that will permeate this game, a rematch in Boston (which will be even more emotional for Brown) and beyond, is the fact that the 76ers' presumed path to playing in May and June also includes the Celtics. Both sit atop the Eastern Conference, having won nine games apiece, with some underlying separation already building on the coast. (Detroit and New York will certainly have something to say about how the final standings shake out; early November is a far cry from finality, but I'm more confident in seeing the demarcation between them and the likes of Toronto, Miami and Atlanta.)

It's why nights like these are important. They offer a window into the psyche of the world's most talented athletes, invoke emotional and mental challenges and push conversations forward. Brown will have more opportunities to even the score against his old coworker, but until he fully settles into his new surroundings, frustrating outings like this won't be outliers.

articles.title: NBA: Boston Celtics best LeBron James' Philadelphia 76ers as Jaylen Brown shares frosty reunion with former team
articles.summary: The Boston Celtics secured a huge 123-101 road win against LeBron James' Philadelphia 76ers to go top of the Eastern Conference; watch the 2026/27 NBA season, including the Christmas Day games and the NBA finals, on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Brown ran into early foul trouble and scored only 13 points in his first game against Boston since the 2024 NBA Finals MVP was traded over the summer to the Sixers. His head-to-head showdown with Tatum was one of the more anticipated early-season matchups with both players refusing to say much about their frosty relationship.

Tatum tried to dap up Brown before the opening tip with a tap on the shoulder and thump on the chest that his former teammate ignored. Tatum shook hands and exchanged a big hug with LeBron James.

Brown picked up two quick fouls in the first quarter and was whistled for his fourth early in the second half.

George, traded for Brown after two seasons with the 76ers, enjoyed the homecoming. He appeared to give the finger in a bowling motion near the visitor's bench after he sank his fourth 3 of the game for a 100-82 lead that pushed the Celtics to their ninth win in 10 games.

The Sixers survived a scare late in the second half when Joel Embiid landed awkwardly and hit the court on a missed layup attempt. The oft-injured big man curled up on the court while VJ Edgecombe dunked over him.

Embiid gingerly ran down the court and hunched over as the halftime horn sounded with the Celtics up 62-51.

Embiid's health has been a career-long issue for him, and the Sixers have declined to play him in back-to-back games. A two-time NBA scoring champion, Embiid has slumped with his shot this season, with no game worse than last Friday in Cleveland when missed all nine shots from the floor and scored only two points.

He had missed 27 of 30 (and 20 consecutive) 3-pointers entering the game. Embiid missed two 3-point attempts in the first half but opened the second with his first 3 since the second game of the season.

Tyrese Maxey led the Sixers with 24 points.

No love lost for Brown as Celtics new order dominate

Brown wasn't a fan of Tatum's brief show of affection, as mentioned above, perhaps a fitting illustration of a frosty relationship that has included radio silence between the two All-Stars since Brown was traded in the summer to the Sixers.

Tatum scored 21 points and outplayed Brown, while George - who the Sixers traded to acquire Brown in the summer - was the star of the night, scoring 14 straight points in the fourth quarter and making six of Boston's 22 3-pointers.

"No headlines about anything like that," Tatum said. "I was just getting ready for the game. Ready for jump ball. Go out there and compete and have some fun and try and get the win."

Brown ran into early foul trouble and scored only 13 points in his first game against Boston since the 2024 NBA Finals MVP was traded. He picked up two quick fouls in the first quarter and was whistled for his fourth early in the second half.

Brown declined to get into his Tatum brush off.

"I'm just focused on doing what's best for my team," Brown said. "Everything else was just, to be honest, I wasn't paying attention."

articles.title: Hamilton state champion diver aims for NCAA title, picks national power
articles.summary: Josi Popma has been one of the best divers in the state. She has made her college decision where she hopes to be one of the country's best.
articles.body:
HAMILTON - Josi Popma might be one of the shortest on the pool deck, but she has delivered some of the biggest performances.

The senior diver stands just 4 feet, 10 inches, but as the defending Division 3 state champion she is setting a giant legacy at Hamilton.

"It definitely puts a lot of pressure on, but I just have to keep doing what I do," Popma said. "I think my height is an advantage because I can spin really fast - I just have to keep it controlled. It gives me confidence because I know I have done it before."

She has done plenty this season, too. Popma broke the Hamilton pool, school and OK Lakeshore Conference record on Saturday, Nov. 7, with a score of 490.15.

"I have been working on my takeoffs and getting higher on my dives," she said.

Hamilton coach Aaron Paskvan said she has become a well-rounded athlete this year.

"Her maturity has been the biggest thing this year. She makes the adjustments and the leadership comes with the maturity," he said. "Her special awareness has helped (team with her fast spins) to feel her spots on her dives."

Popma's performance and potential has received plenty of attention from bigger schools, too.

This week, she made her decision and committed to dive at Grand Valley State.

"I liked the environment of the team. They have really good divers and it felt really welcoming," Popma said. "It just felt like my place to be. It means a lot. I have worked so hard to get there. It is awesome to see that hard work pay off."

The Lakers have a history of great diving, including multiple NCAA champions in recent years.

"It makes me hope that I can get there one day (and win a national title) with some more years of training," Popma said. "I am really excited to see what I can do."

The 2026 North Carolina high school boys basketball season has already arrived as teams across the state can begin action as early as Wednesday, Nov. 11.

Wilmington-area teams enter this winter on the heels of a dazzling 2025-26 season that saw two Port City squads battle for a regional championship and one come just short of a state title.

But the 2026-27 season is a reset for many teams that graduated skilled senior classes. While there may be some new faces, don't be fooled: Wilmington still has plenty of basketball star power.

Now fans have a chance to voice their opinion by voting in the 2026 StarNews Boys Basketball Preseason Player of the Year Poll, which includes 21 nominees from each of the area's 13 squads.

Voting in this poll is fan driven and will run until Tuesday., Nov. 24, at 11:59 p.m. Vote now as many times as you like below.

articles.title: Re-Drafting the 2026 WNBA Draft Class: Where Do Azzi Fudd and Olivia Miles End Up?
articles.summary: The 2026 WNBA Draft featured some of the most shocking twists and turns of any class we've seen.
articles.body:
The 2026 WNBA Draft featured some of the most shocking twists and turns of any class we've seen.

Draft night featured controversy over the first pick, a confusing trade, and unexpected selections from teams that seemed to break completely with most mocks. Despite this group lacking a consensus can't-miss top prospect, a handful of players emerged as surefire stars in their rookie seasons.

Olivia Miles, the second overall pick, took home unanimous Rookie of the Year honors while finishing second in MVP voting. Players like Azzi Fudd, Awa Fam, Kiki Rice, and Flau'jae Johnson looked like future All-Star talents. And many other selectees showcased real WNBA talent, setting the stage for long and productive careers.

With the 2027 Draft Lottery days away, now is a good time to look back on the 2026 draft and evaluate how these players fared in year one. How much would things change if teams could do it over again? Let's redraft this class and see where everyone ends up.

Miles entered the 2026 draft with clear superstar upside, yet she was never really considered a serious option for the Wings at No. 1. There were concerns about Miles' fit with Paige Bueckers, her defensive shortcomings, and her two-point scoring at the WNBA level.

By the Wings' own admission, Azzi Fudd was their sole focus with the top overall pick. While Fudd enjoyed a fantastic rookie season before she hurt her knee, it's fair to wonder whether the Wings regret that decision.

Miles' rookie season was historic in every sense. She broke countless records and became the sixth rookie to make the All-WNBA First Team, averaging 19.8 points, 4.7 rebounds, and 6.0 assists per game. Despite questions about her jumper and efficiency, she posted those numbers with a sparkling .606 true shooting percentage. Miles finished second in MVP voting, the best rookie finish since Candace Parker won the award in 2008.

Unfortunately, Miles finished 2026 on a sour note, with two disastrous playoff performances that culminated in the top-seeded Lynx being unceremoniously swept by New York. Miles wasn't ready for the moment, as all her weaknesses were fully exploited. She needs to add an in-between game and develop midrange/floater counters, be more confident firing from three, and become a threat moving off the ball.

Miles still goes No. 1 here because she's the best talent in the draft. Concerns about her fit with Bueckers have always been overblown; Bueckers loves playing off-ball. There is no doubt that the two players would have formed a dynamic, synergistic backcourt in Dallas.

Minnesota passed on Fam in real life after Miles fell into their laps, but they take her here as a bet on massive upside for the future. Fam entered the draft as a 19-year-old big with tons of professional experience in top European leagues and national competitions.

As a prospect, Fam's calling card was her advanced screen-and-roll ability. In addition to her uncanny understanding of timing and angles, Fam displayed tantalizing skill as a playmaker out of short-roll situations. She continuously made advanced reads and was comfortable calling her own number to score when she had an advantage. Those skills, combined with her athletic, 6'4 frame and fluid mobility, made her a candidate for the top prospect in the draft.

Fam's rookie season was effective but somewhat odd. While she flashed shooting potential as a prospect, Fam's three-ball was considered more of a work in progress coming into the league. But in Seattle last year, Fam was deployed almost exclusively as a five-out spacer, hitting a solid 35% of her threes on 4.3 attempts per game. The fit with Dominique Malonga and Ezi Magbegor (when healthy) wasn't always the cleanest. Head coach Sonia Raman didn't put Fam in positions to showcase many of the skills that made her a great prospect. It certainly doesn't help that Seattle had one of the weakest guard rooms in the league (and no true point guard to speak of).

Apart from fixing her role, Fam needs to improve her defensive rebounding, rim protection, and handle. She made strides as a defender in her rookie season, so the hope is that those other areas can follow. Fam still has limitless potential. Minnesota gets her here as a core piece for both the present and future.

Kiki Rice falling to No. 6 never made any sense. She was clearly a top-3 prospect in this draft, and Toronto likely couldn't believe their luck when they secured her services outside the lottery. The 5'11 UCLA guard proved her doubters wrong in year one, as she has a strong argument for going as high as No. 2 overall in a redraft.

Rice started her rookie season strong before an ankle sprain forced her to miss 16 games. When she returned, Rice picked up right where she left off and ultimately earned All-Rookie team honors. As good as Marina Mabrey was in her first year for the Tempo, Rice proved that she's their franchise player of the future. Coach Sandy Brondello said as much verbatim.

Many Rice skeptics point to her lack of a signature skill. But here's the truth: Rice is good at everything. She can handle the ball and play both guard spots; she's a good spot-up shooter; she's a strong playmaker with good vision and instincts. Rice pressures the rim and finishes well, and she's improving as a pull-up scorer from both the midrange and three-point range.

Defensively, Rice has a lot of room to grow. She was a very good point-of-attack defender at UCLA, but that wasn't the case last year. Rookie guards almost always struggle to adjust to WNBA speed and physicality, though, so Rice should improve there. It's fascinating to think about how she'd fit with Seattle in this spot. The fit with Malonga, Johnson, and Magbegor would be undeniably compelling.

It's hard to imagine a team more in need of Fudd's skills than the Washington Mystics. Washington finished 12th in the WNBA in three-point percentage in 2026 and dead last in three-point attempts in each of the last two seasons. This team desperately needs the elite three-point shooting Fudd brings to the table. They'd be thrilled to get here at fourth overall.

Fudd showed promise in her rookie year as one of the premier "3-and-D" players in the league. Her defensive playmaking was fantastic, averaging 1.7 steals and 0.8 blocks per game as a 5'11 guard. Fudd's slick hands and smart instincts in help led to a positive defensive impact despite some issues at the point of attack, where she often struggled to stay in front of quick guards.

The shooting and gravity from Fudd also shone, though 39.7% on 5.2 three-point attempts per game were both a tad underwhelming for a player of Fudd's marksmanship. Fudd often turned down semi-contested threes to shoot one- or two-dribble pull-up middies. She took 2.8 long midrange shots per game, third in the WNBA among rotation players, and hit those at a blistering 49.4% (per Databallr).

Such proficiency from midrange is great, but Fudd needs to turn at least half of those long middies into threes. It would also be nice to see more self-creation and driving from Fudd, but that probably isn't likely to materialize. As long as she increases her three-point volume and continues to make an impact on defense, she'll be a great player for a long time, provided she stays healthy.

Fudd had arthroscopic right knee surgery in August, ending her season. That knee has now sustained four surgeries and at least four other issues that caused Fudd to miss time. Hopefully, this latest procedure cleaned some things up so Fudd can get healthy and minimize future issues.

Johnson's Original Draft Position: No. 8

Chicago could have selected Johnson (and Kiki Rice!) for real on draft night, but opted for Jaquez instead. Johnson was then involved in one of the more confusing trades in WNBA Draft history; Golden State took her at No. 8 and traded her to Seattle a half hour later for No. 14 and a future second-round pick. It's still unclear why Golden State did this, but hey, they won the title.

Whatever the Valkyries were cooking, it greatly benefited the Storm, as Johnson had a terrific rookie season. Johnson was second to Miles in rookie scoring at 14.9 points per game. She had a positive impact on both ends for a horrible Storm team. Seattle posted a -4.1 net rating with Johnson on the floor compared to a -15.7 mark with her off. So, while Johnson didn't make the Storm a good team, her presence at least made it not historically awful.

Johnson is a talented bucket-getter with a great handle, elite athleticism, and a pretty jumper. She flashed legit two-way upside in her rookie season, but she still has a ton of room to grow. Johnson must improve her efficiency, as she wasn't particularly effective from any area of the floor. The three-point shooting (29.6%) was baffling, although that should bounce back in a big way next year. Johnson also tends to avoid her left hand entirely at the rim, leading to poor finishing. Apart from the shooting struggles, Johnson's overall processing and decision-making leave a bit to be desired.

It sounds like Johnson has a lot to improve on, which is true. But her raw skills and physical profile are special. She performed admirably on a bad team en route to All-Rookie honors in 2026.

The Mystics took Betts fourth overall, despite a crowded frontcourt situation, because she was the best available player on their board. As a result, Betts played a reserve role as a rookie behind stars Shakira Austin and Kiki Iriafen. In this redraft, Betts gets to join a brand-new expansion team and start at center.

Betts performed adequately as a rookie backup, providing solid post scoring, rebounding, and defense. Washington posted a suffocating 97.8 defensive rating with Betts on the floor, the best mark of any rotation player on the team. The skills that made Betts such a dominant college player were on full display, as Washington didn't overexpose her in year one.

Betts still struggles as a screen-and-roll player and needs to find a way to add value there. It's great when she can score on a deep seal or offensive rebound, but to be a plus offensive player in today's game, the screening needs to come along. The jumper could be a lost cause, though Betts doesn't need to shoot to be a good player.

The defensive upside for Betts remains sky-high. She has some of the best rim-protecting instincts in the league, while her mobility isn't bad for her massive height. If the offense comes around, star outcomes are still on the table.

Nothing changes here; Portland has reportedly been enamored with Martín for a long time. She's also the best talent on the board. Martín is a 20-year-old Spanish point guard with a lot of flair to her game. She didn't play in the WNBA last year, opting to stay in Spain and play for Avenida.

The mainstream basketball world was introduced to Martín in a big way during the 2026 FIBA World Cup, as she enjoyed a massive breakout tournament. Martín averaged 17.5 points and 4.2 assists per game on 55/45/90 shooting splits and was likely the best player in the entire competition. Spain earned the bronze medal with Martín leading the charge.

Martín is a dynamic 5'9 guard with incredible vision and passing ability. She's at her best maneuvering out of ball screens, using her live dribble and vision to find open shooters and drive when there's an advantage. Martín has been up-and-down with the jumper. Her finishing needs improvement, but she's easy to project as a valuable offensive player with a rare set of creation skills.

Defensively, Martín's size and extremely slender frame create issues. She is also a pretty poor athlete who struggles to contain dribble penetration. It's hard to imagine Martín avoiding becoming a liability on that end, though she does compete.

In Portland, they already employ a high-usage, pick-and-roll-spamming point guard with a streaky jumper and questionable defensive utility. It's fair to wonder how Carla Leite and Martín can coexist, or if they can share the floor for extended stretches. Still, even with those concerns, Martín has too much talent not to heavily factor into Portland's future plans.

8. Golden State Valkyries, Gabriela Jaquez

Jaquez was connected to Golden State a lot in the pre-draft process; most saw this spot as the highest she would go on draft night. Of course, the Chicago Sky shocked the world by taking Jaquez fifth overall. Golden State responded by punting their first-round pick altogether.

Much of the industry considered the Jaquez pick a reach. A year later, it's safe to say they were correct. Even so, the 6'0 wing is a solid basketball player who contributes in many areas. It starts with her motor; Jaquez is always going to play harder than most other players on the floor. Everything she does is with intention-- she cuts hard, plays physical defense, and sprints up and down the court.

All of that effort adds up to winning plays on both ends. At the same time, Jaquez struggles with many macro skills of the game. She isn't a real shooter (27% from three on just 1.8 attempts per game last year), which is her biggest downfall. If Jaquez could be relied upon to knock down threes, she'd have a much more viable role.

But without the shooting threat, there isn't enough offensive skill to go on. Jaquez isn't a creator with the ball. She's not tall or strong enough to bang with WNBA wings. She isn't an efficient scorer from anywhere. While Jaquez adds some defensive value with her effort and activity, she's not good enough on that end to make up for the offensive shortcomings.

If Jaquez got drafted to Golden State, she'd probably shoot six threes per game at a 36% clip in Natalie Nakase's system. In fact, it wouldn't be shocking to see her end up there eventually and become the perfect plug-and-play utility wing. Until then, we'll see if she can take a step forward in Chicago next season.

Johnson's Original Draft Position: No. 10

Washington could have taken Johnson on draft night, but reached for Dugalić instead. Although Johnson didn't have a particularly strong statistical rookie season in Indiana, she flashed the winning qualities that make her such a unique player.

Glance at Johnson's averages last year and you might think she doesn't even deserve to be drafted in the first round here. She averaged just a touch over 3 points per game and shot 23% from three as an undersized point guard. So, what gives? How is she any good?

Well, Johnson may be 5'8, but her near-6'3 wingspan makes up for much of that size deficit. Combined with her strength and athleticism, that lets her wreak havoc as a point-of-attack defender.

While her offensive profile raises genuine concerns, Johnson doesn't need to score to be effective. She's out there to find teammates, move the ball, and attack the gaps. At the same time, you'd like her to hit an open three or pressure the rim out of ball screens. If those skills develop, Johnson will play for a long time in this league. If not, she should carve out a role as a defensive-minded gadget player.

In last year's playoffs, Johnson elevated her game, averaging 7.3 points per game on 59% shooting from the field against the Aces. Johnson also stepped up in big games throughout her college career because she's a winning player who shines in pressure moments. As Johnson continues to improve, we'll see if the statistics start to catch up with the intangibles.

10. Indiana Fever, Charlisse Leger-Walker

Leger-Walker's Original Draft Position : No. 18

The Team Formerly Known as the Connecticut Sun scored a big-time steal with Leger-Walker in the second round of this draft. CLW had a solid rookie year on an awful Sun team and looks like a legitimate backup point guard for years to come. Here, she goes to Indiana to give their bench a boost behind Caitlin Clark.

Leger-Walker's value starts with her playmaking and processing abilities. She plays at her own pace and makes smart reads out of ball screens, organizing the offense and setting up teammates. Leger-Walker isn't much of a scorer. Her three-ball was streaky in 2026, but she adds just enough juice to keep defenses honest.

As a poor athlete at 5'10, Leger-Walker isn't giving you much on the defensive end. She does grab the occasional steal (0.8 per game last year) and is strong enough to compete against mismatches. As she matures, she should be able to become a neutral presence on defense.

While there isn't a ton of upside with Leger-Walker, there's a good chance she settles into a backup point guard role for whichever team needs one. For a second-round pick, that's a very positive outcome.

Since Washington misses out on Lauren Betts in this redraft, they snag their backup center in Okot here. The 6'6 South Carolina big had a solid rookie season in Atlanta, showcasing the athletic tools that made her such an intriguing prospect.

Okot was used sparingly for the Finals-bound Dream, but there were some encouraging signs. Her 22.1% rebounding rate was in the 99th percentile league-wide (per Her Hoops Stats). She provided some much-needed rim protection in her sporadic playing time.

Apart from those positives, Okot couldn't stay on the floor because of poor processing on both ends. She struggled with turnovers and decision-making in college at South Carolina. That continued in her rookie year. Okot stops the ball too often and doesn't react well to the defense. On the other end of the floor, Okot didn't hold up defending in space and fouled too much.

Okot didn't start playing basketball until 2020, so she's a bit behind the developmental 8-ball. There's every reason to believe she can develop into a very solid pro, especially with her elite physical traits.

12. Connecticut Sun (Houston Comets), Nell Angloma

Angloma's Original Draft Position: No. 12

Another pick remains status quo, as the young Angloma still makes perfect sense for the rebuilding Sun/Comets at this spot. At 21 years old, Angloma retains a ton of enticing potential after a largely uneventful rookie season.

Angloma came over from France and played the full season in Connecticut, averaging a meager 4.4 points and 1.9 rebounds per game in a reserve role. As a prospect, the sell for Angloma was this: a strong, physical defender who gets downhill and draws fouls. Sure, she can't shoot at all, and the overall feel is a bit worrisome, but her standout skills offer a pretty safe floor.

In year one, Angloma's strengths were on display, albeit in a diminished capacity. Connecticut's defensive rating was 3.2 better with Angloma on the floor. She posted a stellar .436 free-throw rate. Angloma is a decent finisher at the rim with a strong left hand, so there's some hope she can leverage that into more consistent offensive production off drives. If the three-ball ever comes around to even average levels, this is a real player. There aren't many wings her size with this combination of strength and quickness.

Bühner had a nice rookie season in Portland after initially signing a development contract as a second-round pick. The 22-year-old German international was rewarded for her solid play with a full-time deal in early May and became a rotation fixture for the upstart Fire.

Bühner is a classic finesse forward who likes to operate as an offensive hub and score in the intermediate areas of the floor. Though her three-point shot was considered a question mark as a prospect, Bühner hit a respectable 35% of her attempts from distance in 2026. Even better, she posted a .503 three-point rate, demonstrating a willingness to act as a spacer. Drawing closeouts opens up the floor for Bühner to showcase her craft and court vision, as there were glimpses of that throughout year one.

Athletic limitations and tweener size limit Bühner on defense, but she's pretty strong and did a decent job playing her role in Sarama's scheme. In this redraft, she's a nice complement to Atlanta's physical, defensive frontcourt room.

Morgan's Original Draft Position: No. 32

That's right, we've got a third-round pick crashing the redraft party. Morgan was a better point guard prospect than real-life selection Taina Mair. It doesn't make sense that she fell to the third round. After the Chicago Sky selected her, they cut Morgan in training camp before she eventually worked her way into a development contract with the Sparks. In August, Los Angeles converted that into a standard deal, as Morgan had a nice run of games to close the season.

Morgan is a savvy playmaker with good athleticism and vision. She gets to the rim, finishes at a high level, and finds teammates off drives. There's not much else to her game. She can be a little turnover-prone, but there's value in a competent creator who can pressure the rim and organize the offense.

If Morgan can add a somewhat respectable jumper and avoid being targeted on defense, she should stay in the league. The fit with Seattle here makes a ton of sense, as that group desperately needs a floor general to set things up for their dynamic bigs.

15. Connecticut Sun (Houston Comets), Shay Ciezki

Ciezki's Original Draft Position: Undrafted

Forget the third round; we're closing things out with an undrafted gem. It turns out being a 5'7 off-guard works against your WNBA prospects, as Ciezki learned the hard way on draft night. However, none of that is Ciezki's fault. All she did her senior year was put up one of the most efficient, high-volume scoring seasons in college basketball history. The Mercury signed her to a development contract post-draft, cut her a month later, and then ultimately brought her back on a standard deal to close out the season.

Ciezki took 652 three-pointers in college and hit 264 of them (40.5%). A large percentage of those shots were self-created. Ciezki showcased that ability in her WNBA cup of coffee. Ciezki can also hit catch-and-shoot threes and midrange shots, making her one of the most complete jump shooters in the sport. Pair that with a good handle and creativity in the pick-and-roll, and you've got a dynamic combo guard with explosive offensive potential.

Sadly, Ciezki's size remains an issue. She will always have to be schemed around on defense. Her height also limits her playmaking on the other end. Still, there aren't many shot-making talents like Ciezki in the league. That should allow her to hang around as a bench sparkplug for a bit.

articles.title: Ranking Top 10 NBA Trade Targets Right Now, Plus Landing Spots
articles.summary: The 2026-27 NBA season is young, but teams now have data.
articles.body:
The 2026-27 NBA season is young, but teams now have data.

Probably not enough to make big-picture proclamations, but enough to start getting a feel for what is and isn't possible with their talent on hand.

As those assessments get more detailed—typically closer to the first-quarter mark—that's when the trade market springs to life. And you better believe front offices are already plotting paths for the directions they might take once this installment of #TradeSZN reaches a hardwood near you.

We're just getting an early start on the path-plotting process by identifying ( and ranking! ) the top players on or reasonably connected to the trade market. While the rankings are subjective, they do include everything from established ability and projected immediate impact to age, contract status, and anything else that can make a trade commodity more or less valuable.

The Kings are clearly all-in on Darius Acuff Jr., their 19-year-old rookie who's averaging more shots than everyone not named Luka Dončić or Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. They're also out on their incumbent veteran core and probably have been for a while. And Sabonis, for the record, might welcome a change, too.

Sabonis has a rich resume featuring three All-Star selections, a slew of overstuffed stat lines and a general level of efficiency that speaks to his polish and processing. He also has a reputation as being more of a floor-raiser than a ceiling-pusher, since his limitations can get (and have been) exposed in the playoffs.

He won't have universal appeal, in other words, because teams seeking stars and with the assets to acquire them will aim higher. But for desperate shoppers on a tight trade budget, Sabonis could be perfect. And he could be a solid get for anyone aiming to up its talent level without depleting its draft stock.

Possible landing spots: Atlanta Hawks, Phoenix Suns, Toronto Raptors

Before the ink dried on the two-year, $44 million pact Powell signed with Chicago this summer, the veteran scorer emerged as one of the league's most logical trade candidates. The Bulls are thinking years down the line, while the 33-year-old Powell (34 in March) is very much playing for the present.

This felt like free agency's most obvious marriage of convenience. Powell pocketed a hefty sum, as he should have following back-to-back seasons of averaging 21-plus points. The Bulls gained a valuable veteran voice and an offensive asset to help give their young core guidance and on-court support. And neither side would be glued to the partnership for long, since the second season is a team option .

Chatter has already started about Powell, and it will only increase as the league creeps closer to the trade deadline. It would help if he was scoring more efficiently (39.8 percent shooting, 30.9 percent from three), but his track record suggests he'll bounce back, especially when he gets back around more established talent.

Possible landing spots: Boston Celtics, Detroit Pistons, Golden State Warriors

When Herro joined his hometown Bucks in this summer's Giannis Antetokounmpo blockbuster, he had high hopes for the club. He told The Athletic's Eric Nehm , "I think we're going to be better than people anticipate," then added, "We're gonna be good."

The Bucks are decidedly not good: 1-9 on the season with a disastrously awful (and 28th-ranked) minus-13.1 net rating . Herro, to his credit, has been pretty good (21.4 points, 4.3 assists and 3.1 three-pointers), but the roster around him just isn't ready to compete.

That will get outside teams talking about him. It almost assuredly already has. Between his offensive punch and expiring $33 million salary, he's a stretch-run-boost waiting to happen for the right team.

Possible landing spots: Detroit Pistons, Orlando Magic, Toronto Raptors

2027 NFL Free Agency Big Board After Trade Deadline 🔢

While the Nets technically have no incentive to tank now (Houston holds swap rights to Brooklyn's 2027 first-round pick), they clearly lack the talent to compete. They have twice as many double-digit losses (four) as any-digit wins (two) and have encountered major malfunctions at both ends.

With the Nets potentially misfiring on a handful of first-round picks in recent years, there is an urgent and obvious need for more throws at the dartboard. Porter, a proven shotmaker and support scorer with championship experience, could be their path toward getting some.

While he is overpaid, he comes with no long-term commitments, since his $40.8 million salary is expiring. For those who can make the cap numbers work, he is the kind of spacer and bucket-getter who could help an offense jump from good to great.

Possible landing spots: Detroit Pistons, Orlando Magic, San Antonio Spurs

A healthy version of Davis remains a dominant force. Just ask the Detroit Pistons, who just found themselves on the wrong end of his 44-point, 13-rebound eruption.

But Davis' struggles staying healthy are well-documented, and they certainly won't get easier to manage as he probes deeper into his 30s. They also create questions about his desire for top dollar , which is one of several reasons—along with frustration and timeline—to wonder whether his time with Washington will last much longer.

Buzzy talks about a possible return to the Los Angeles Lakers don't have legs , but Davis could be a massive get for the right shopper. Whether co-starring with a currently solo star or anchoring the interior for a could-be contender, he is the kind of player who could— if healthy asterisk forever attached —tip the scales of the championship race.

Possible landing spots: Golden State Warriors, Phoenix Suns, Toronto Raptors

While the Clippers split from Kawhi Leonard this summer, they haven't really shifted into youth-movement mode yet. And, honestly, flipping that switch will be tricky given their severe shortage of draft capital .

Add a sluggish, uninspiring start to this season to the equation, and it feels like all breadcrumbs could lead toward a blockbuster subtraction. Garland's creation, shot-making and efficiency could all boost a win-now club, and L.A. doesn't look like it'll be winning any time soon. It also probably needs the picks he could deliver in a deal to even start turning the corner.

Because Garland is youngish (26 until late January), he could attract both win-now and win-pretty-soon shoppers. That will help his market. What could it hurt, though, are concerns of availability and defensive viability, plus the need for a new (almost certainly super costly) contract by 2028.

Possible landing spots: Chicago Bulls, Memphis Grizzlies, Phoenix Suns

The partnership between Irving and Cooper Flagg has been both wildly entertaining and absurdly effective ( plus-13.6 net rating across 190 minutes). Seeing them in action makes you almost forget the near-constant trade speculation surrounding the former, which is exactly how Irving would prefer it.

"I let the team know out of my own mouth that these trade rumors, anything that's going on with me, do not let this infiltrate our locker room," Irving told reporters . "Don't let this get in the way of what we have building here."

That's the kind of leadership teams should want from a floor general. It's also powerless to stop that string of trade chatter, which feels unavoidable given the timeline crater separating the 19-year-old Flagg from the 34-year-old Irving.

The uber-creative lead guard would work best on a team hoping to contend right now and feeling like it might be one offensive upgrade away from doing it. He isn't for everyone—older, often injured and uncertain for the long haul (player option for 2027-28)—but he is very much for the suitors that make sense.

Possible landing spots: Atlanta Hawks, Detroit Pistons, Miami Heat

The Magic clearly sought out change when they dismissed former coach Jamahl Mosley this offseason after three consecutive first-round exits. This can't be the change it had in mind: a drop from pretty good to putrid (2-7 with the league's seventh-worst net rating ).

Injuries haven't helped, but this core has long been questioned about its composition. So, a clean bill of health wouldn't definitively shore up a defense that isn't defending or an offense that's struggling to make shots from anywhere.

The Magic might have to rethink their long-term (and high-dollar) commitment to overlapping wings Wagner and Paolo Banchero. It could honestly squeeze either out, and the market would be thrilled with either outcome.

Wagner is older and slightly less productive than his costar, and he's had some availability issues of late (94 games played the past two seasons combined), so he could have trouble climbing any higher up the rankings. Still, his blend of polish and potential could appeal both to contenders eyeing a second or third star or rebuilders who are eager to find their next centerpiece.

Possible landing spots: Brooklyn Nets, Golden State Warriors, San Antonio Spurs

If the Magic interpret their sluggish start as a sign to change their formula, then one of their starring, ball-dominant forwards has to go. It could be Wagner, but it could just as easily be Banchero, who has star-level production but not the efficiency or impact of a superstar.

Maybe he just isn't what folks envisioned when he arrived as the top pick of the 2022 draft. Or perhaps Orlando just isn't the right environment to bring out his best as a 6'10", 250-pound primary scorer and secondary shot-creator.

Not all teams will be willing pay a premium to find out. Not when Banchero is basically a few injury-riddled weeks into a five-year, $239.2 million contract.

For folks desperate to find a difference-maker, though, he has the building-block package of size, skill, stardom and ceiling. If he's already this productive in a less than ideal setting (career 22.4 points, 7.4 rebounds and 4.8 assists), the imaginaton runs wild thinking what he might do with a roster more tailored to his strengths and weaknesses.

Possible landing spots: Brooklyn Nets, Phoenix Suns, Sacramento Kings

1. Trey Murphy III, New Orleans Pelicans

Among players on or near the trade market, Murphy might come closest to offering universal appeal. It's not that he's the best player listed here or the most decorated, but rather that he is (relatively) affordable, scheme- and role-versatile and aged just right to offer established production and a bit of untapped potential.

You could talk yourself into half of the league qualifying as logical landing spots for Murphy. Maybe more. Which probably explains why the Pelicans have held firm on such a steep asking price, reported this summer by HoopsHype's Michael Scotto to be "the equivalent of...three first-round picks."

That price tag is rich, but there are teams that can cover it and would for an athletic big wing who adds value on both ends of the floor and possesses an all-purpose set of supplemental skills.

Muraphy isn't a game-changer, but rather a game-enhancer. Any midseason move involving him would be light on disruption and heavy on impact.

Possible landing spots: Boston Celtics, Oklahoma City Thunder, San Antonio Spurs

articles.title: A 5-Step Blueprint To Luka Dončić Winning NBA MVP
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers are better than expected, jumping out to a 10-2 start for an early hold on first place in the Western Conference.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers are better than expected, jumping out to a 10-2 start for an early hold on first place in the Western Conference.

Luka Dončić scored only 32 points in his team's 124-114 win over the Hawks in Atlanta on Monday, dropping his average below 40 to 39.3 per game. He still leads the NBA in scoring by a sizable margin.

With Dončić now in his ninth NBA season, what will it take for him to finally win league MVP?

The NBA's Most Valuable Player award usually goes to the best player on the best team. Dončić's greatest challengers are Victor Wembanyama (San Antonio Spurs) and current back-to-back winner Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (Oklahoma City Thunder).

Before the season, both teams were widely considered the favorites in the West, with the Lakers grouped somewhere among second-tier contenders like the Houston Rockets, Minnesota Timberwolves, and Denver Nuggets.

The Thunder's early spate of injuries bolsters Gilgeous-Alexander's chance at the three-peat, should he lead his team to the top seed in the West despite Jalen Williams (leg), Cason Wallace (shoulder), and Chet Holmgren (knee) being out for months, if not the entire season. (Holmgren should return in early 2027.)

But Dončić's most significant threat is Wembanyama, who is putting up video-game numbers, including 52 points, 24 rebounds, and eight blocks in a recent win over the Dallas Mavericks.

The Lakers need to finish ahead of the Spurs and Thunder to give Dončić his best shot. That translates to support from head coach JJ Redick, teammates like Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler, and the front office to address roster needs as they arise.

Dončić's 39.3 points per game is almost nine points higher than the NBA's No. 2 scorer, Steph Curry, who is averaging 30.6 with the Golden State Warriors. Right behind him are Wembanyama (30.1) and Gilgeous-Alexander (29.9).

These are the elite of the elite, and Dončić is lapping them. And more importantly, the Lakers keep winning.

Luka-ball got the Dallas Mavericks to the 2024 NBA Finals, but he finished third in MVP voting that regular season, behind Nikola Jokić (Denver Nuggets) and Gilgeous-Alexander. He needs to dominate the league individually while his team does the same.

That formula has clicked through the first few weeks of the season; both need to maintain it for the next five months.

For Dončić, the easier of the two is the scoring title. He's an all-time-level talent on offense. But that alone won't be enough, as 2023-24 showed.

The physical burden of scoring over 30 points a night has led to some of history's best players taking plays off on defense. Dončić has been guilty of that before, but through the start of the 2026-27 campaign, he's playing some of the best defense of his career.

Instead of hiding him on opposing teams' non-scorers, Redick is asking Dončić to actively guard opposing wings. He lacks foot speed, but he makes up for it with how quickly he can mentally process the opposing team's attack. Dončić is averaging 2.0 steals and a career-high 0.8 blocks per game.

As a team, the Lakers are competing at a high level defensively. Acquiring Walker Kessler from the Utah Jazz in July gave the Lakers a proper rim protector. Neither Dončić nor Reaves is a defensive stopper, but the franchise has a long list of players willing to fight, including Ziaire Williams, Matisse Thybulle, Jake LaRavia, Quentin Grimes, Adou Thiero, and Jarred Vanderbilt.

The Lakers are among the league's top-scoring teams. If they can maintain above-average defense, with Dončić part of the solution and not the problem, the best record in the West is attainable.

Per NBA rules, Dončić will only be eligible for MVP if he reaches the 65-games-played threshold. The league made an exception last year, when Dončić missed a pair of December games for the birth of his second daughter.

Regardless, the Lakers need their best player on the court nearly every night, although Reaves carried the scoring load when Dončić sat out against the Detroit Pistons. Missing games is a double-edged sword: either the team will fall out of the race for the No. 1 seed, or it won't. If Reaves can keep the franchise winning at the same clip without Dončić, that waters down the MVP case.

L.A.'s early pattern is to rest Dončić for one game of each back-to-back. If he plays both ends of the all-home back-to-backs and avoids nicks and bruises (and more serious injuries), 70-plus games is a reasonable expectation.

It's more reality than cliche: an NBA season is a marathon, not a sprint.

Managing an 82-game regular season is an exhausting task. Beyond what the players need to handle, the coaching staff and front office must be ready to adapt to the inevitable hurdles ahead.

From injuries to slumps to design flaws, the franchise needs to keep Dončić and the squad on a winning track. Before the back-to-back wins over the Pistons and Hawks, the Lakers had a relatively light schedule based on opponent strength and travel.

Can the team maintain its current pace on both sides of the ball, and if not, what then?

The Lakers lack significant draft capital but still may be in play for roster upgrades ahead of the Feb. 11 trade deadline. Top on the wish list would be a backup center who can reduce the drop-off in rim protection when Kessler sits.

The goal shouldn't be to play for the MVP award, but to win enough games to capture the No. 1 seed. Dončić will be the featured scorer, so keeping him healthy and supported will put the franchise in the best position to win.

Everything has lined up early in the year, but the team needs to brace for the challenges ahead and take the necessary steps to compete at the highest level.

Email Eric Pincus at eric.pincus@gmail.com and follow him on X @EricPincus .

articles.title: Paul George Explains Giving Middle Finger to Fan in Viral Video After Celtics' Win vs. 76ers
articles.summary: Paul George's return to Philadelphia was a rousing success on the court as he dropped 36 points to lead the Boston Celtics to a 123-101 win over the 76ers on Tuesday, but there was an apparent fan interaction at one point that had everyone talking.
articles.body:
Paul George's return to Philadelphia was a rousing success on the court as he dropped 36 points to lead the Boston Celtics to a 123-101 win over the 76ers on Tuesday, but there was an apparent fan interaction at one point that had everyone talking.

After George was seen giving a middle finger to the crowd during the game, he explained there was a fan "being an a--hole" who dropped the ball on the ground instead of passing it back to him that prompted him to flip the bird.

The environment in Philadelphia is generally heightened when the Celtics are in town because there's so much history between the two teams, but Tuesday was unique even by those standards.

It was the first Celtics-76ers game since the offseason trade that sent George to Boston in exchange for Jaylen Brown.

George's two-year run in Philadelphia was generally regarded as a disappointment. He only played in 78 games after signing a four-year, $212 million deal as a free agent in the summer of 2024.

Most of George's limited playing time was due to injuries, but he was also suspended for 25 games in January due to violating the NBA/NBPA anti-drug program.

George has enjoyed a resurgence so far this season with the Celtics. Tuesday was arguably his best game with 36 points on 14-of-22 shooting (6-of-11 from three) in 30 minutes against his former team.

The 36 points would have been George's second-best scoring game from his entire run with Philadelphia. He put up 39 in a 153-131 win over the Washington Wizards on April 1 last season.

Boston has won four consecutive games and sits at 9-2 overall to move into first place in the Eastern Conference standings.

articles.title: Jaylen Brown Explains Ignoring Jayson Tatum in Viral Video in 1st Celtics-76ers Game Since Trade
articles.summary: Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum both discussed the awkward interaction they had prior to the Boston Celtics' 123-101 road win over the Philadelphia 76ers on Tuesday night.
articles.body:
Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum both discussed the awkward interaction they had prior to the Boston Celtics' 123-101 road win over the Philadelphia 76ers on Tuesday night.

Before the tip-off, Tatum approached Brown and patted him on the arm and chest, but Brown didn't appear to acknowledge him:

When asked about the notion that he was ignoring his former teammate, Brown told reporters, "I'm just focused on coming out and doing what's best for my team. Everything else was just—to be honest, I wasn't paying attention. But credit to Jayson, he played well tonight. Credit to the Celtics, they executed, they shot the hell out of the ball and they were the better team tonight."

Tatum didn't offer many specifics when asked about the viral moment, telling reporters, "Listen, like I said, no headlines about anything like that. I was just getting ready for the game. Ready for jump ball. Go out there, compete, have some fun and try to get a win."

Brown and Tatum were teammates in Boston for nine years, winning an NBA championship together in 2024.

However, the Celtics made the surprising decision to move on from Brown this past offseason, trading him to the Sixers in exchange for Paul George and draft picks.

That naturally led to speculation regarding potential issues between Tatum and Brown, and whether Tatum may have played a role in Brown's departure.

Last month, Brown raised some eyebrows when he commented a "cap" emoji in response to a video of Tatum saying he was "just as much caught off guard as the rest of the world" by the Celtics' decision to trade Brown:

That led to questions for both players about their relationship, and Tatum told reporters there was "no beef."

Brown said the same, but added some caveats as well, telling reporters , "Jayson's a great guy. Like I said, great family, hell of a basketball player, hell of a PR team. There's no beef, but it'll be a little lamb chop."

Tuesday represented the first game between Boston and Philadelphia since the trade, and the Celtics flexed their muscles in what was their signature win of the season thus far.

Tatum put up 21 points, six rebounds, four assists and two blocks, compared to Brown's 13 points, five rebounds, two assists and two steals.

The true star of the game was George, who went off on his former team with a game-high 36 points on 14-of-22 shooting, plus five rebounds and one assist.

Boston moved into sole possession of first place in the Eastern Conference with a 9-2 record, while the Sixers are second with a 9-3 mark.

The next meeting between Tatum's Celtics and Brown's 76ers is set for Jan. 21, and it will mark Brown's highly anticipated return to Boston.

articles.title: Jayson Tatum Says Celtics-76ers 'Felt Like a F--king Finals Game' Amid Matchup vs. Jaylen Brown
articles.summary: Jayson Tatum didn't take any offense to Jaylen Brown appearing to ignore him prior to the start of Tuesday's game between the Boston Celtics and Philadelphia 76ers.
articles.body:
Jayson Tatum didn't take any offense to Jaylen Brown appearing to ignore him prior to the start of Tuesday's game between the Boston Celtics and Philadelphia 76ers.

Following the Celtics' 123-101 victory in Philadelphia, Tatum told reporters Tuesday "felt like a f--king Finals game" because of how intense the atmosphere in Xfinity Mobile Arena was, but the night was "not about" him against Brown.

The main source of tension seemed to exist between Tatum and Brown, with the latter seemingly not acknowledging his former teammate prior to tipoff.

Tatum did have the biggest highlight of the night when he drove the lane and dunked over LeBron James in the third quarter.

In addition to the Brown-Tatum storyline, there was also the animosity from 76ers fans toward Paul George after his difficult two-season run with Philadelphia that ended when he was traded to the Celtics as part of the Brown deal.

George got heated at one point late in the game that he gave a fan in the stands a middle finger because he took exception to the fan dropping the ball on the ground rather than passing it back to him after it went into the stands.

Tatum and the Celtics ultimately got the last laugh with perhaps their best win of the season so far. Their 123 points scored was the most allowed by Philadelphia all season.

The Celtics have now won four straight games with their last three all decided by at least 20 points. Their 9-2 record is the best in the Eastern Conference and they are one game behind the Los Angeles Lakers in the win column for the best record in the NBA.

articles.title: El método Lorena Torres: así trabaja la española que ha conquistado la WNBA
articles.standfirst: La directora de rendimiento y del departamento médico de las campeonas Golden State Valkyries cuenta a MARCA las claves del éxito de un equipo con sólo dos años de existencia
articles.summary: La directora de rendimiento y del departamento médico de las campeonas Golden State Valkyries cuenta a MARCA las claves del éxito de un equipo con sólo dos años de existencia
articles.body: Han pasado 10 días desde que las Golden State Valkyries ganaran la WNBA, pero el subidón de las campeonas no ha bajado. Lorena Torres, directora de rendimiento y del departamento médico de la franquicia, y el resto aún no terminan de creerse su propio éxito. "Desde el lunes hemos estado haciendo reuniones y todo el mundo estamos como: '¿En serio? ¿Esto ha pasado?'. Estamos aún un poco como en shock", cuenta durante sus vacaciones activas, pues ya planifica la próxima temporada. Las Valkyries dieron una campanada histórica conquistando el título, porque "la gente no es consciente de que hace dos años esto no existía y ahora estamos batiendo récords". Campeonas de la WNBA en su segundo año de vida y el equipo femenino más valioso del deporte mundial. Antes de ganar el angustioso séptimo partido de la final a las Atlanta Dream, se estimaba que estaba en unos 1.000 millones de dólares. Ahora, con la vitola de campeonas, aún más. Y Torres ha estado ahí desde que la franquicia dio sus primeros pasos hacia el éxito. Aún recuerda que estaba trabajando en Madrid para la agencia de representación You First, ahora integrada en Gersh, cuando recibió una llamada de un conocido que le iba a recomendar para trabajar en un futuro equipo de WNBA. "Era la primera vez que tenía un trabajo con fines de semana y estaba muy a gusto", cuenta. "Le dije: 'Puedes dar mi nombre, pero no creo que vaya". ¡Lo que se habría perdido! La general manager Ohemaa Nyanin contactó con ella, hicieron una serie de entrevistas y le compraron un billete a Estambul para verse allí. Torres les hizo una presentación de su proyecto y a las pocas horas le hicieron una propuesta que no podía rechazar. Tendría vía libre para montar su departamento y, lo más importante, la confianza de quien manda. "Mi jefa me dijo : 'Tienen que creer en ti antes de darles tiempo a poder creer en ti'. La gente tiene que confiar y yo me he sentido muy valorada", afirma. Además, iba a trabajar para la marca Golden State, una de las más reconocidas del deporte mundial. El reto era mayúsculo, pues era empezar de la nada. "El año pasado tuve que fichar a fisios, preparadores físicos, nutricionistas, psicólogos, chefs..., hacer que la gente se aclarara entre ellos, que se comunicaran, que nos coordináramos entre nosotros, que yo me coordinara con los entrenadores... Todo el engranaje fue complicado", cuenta. Al ser una franquicia de nueva creación, la plantilla se formó a través del draft de expansión, donde se escogen jugadoras que otros equipos acceden a dejar marchar. No hay grandes nombres. La internacional francesa Gabby Williams es la referencia. "La clave era tener banquillo. Gestionamos lo máximo posible al cinco titular, teniendo unas suplentes que nos van a aguantar el marcador y que son buenas para poder llegar con energía y lo más sanas posibles a los playoffs", explica. El plan, en el que también tenía que creer la entrenadora Natalie Nakase, salió bien. Trabajando a destajo, pero en un segundo plano, Torres ha manejado los hilos de las Valkyries. "Yo tengo un rol más de gestión. Mi equipo, que es fantástico, es el que trabaja ejecutando mi visión: el físio es el que hace los tratamientos, el preparador físico es el que está haciendo las pesas con ellas, el sports scientist es el que les pone el chip y descarga los datos... Nos reunimos a primera hora de la mañana y yo soy la que les digo lo que deben hacer dependiendo de las necesidades y el estado de cada jugadora", desvela sobre su forma de trabajar con siete profesionales a su cargo. En sus manos también estaba la carga física de las jugadoras, si la entrenadora podía apretar más o debía echar el freno, la duración de las sesiones de trabajo, los descansos, si se quedaban a dormir en la ciudad después de un partido a domicilio o si regresaban a casa... "Yo en el día a día ni lo pensaba, trabajando como una loca, apagando fuegos...", bromea antes de agradecer las palabras de Williams tras ganar el título: "A nadie le gusta que le digan que va a jugar menos, pero se alegraba porque se había sentido bien cuando se tenía que sentir bien". Ahí queda su MVP de la final. Torres practicó natación sincronizada hasta que tuvo que elegir entre la piscina y los estudios. Tiró por lo segundo. Conviviendo siempre con el alto rendimiento tras pasar por la Residencia Joaquín Blume, hizo INEF y desde entonces no ha dejado de estudiar y encadenar másters. Dio sus primeros pasos en la preparación física en la cantera de la sección de baloncesto del Barcelona. Con el balón naranja ha estado casi toda su carrera. Ha trabajado con la Federación Española, los Spurs y los Sixers. "He tenido algunos entornos más difíciles de gestionar por ser mujer, pero en general lo he sabido llevar y con la experiencia se endurece la piel y tienes más tablas", afirma. En España no se termina de apostar por disciplinas y formas de trabajar como las que ella domina. Salvo excepciones, no existe la inversión económica ni se termina de creer en ello. "Habría que preguntar a los clubes por qué no existe una figura como la mía que sí está en otros muchos sitios del mundo, pero es que si los equipos todavía se creen que yo soy una preparadora física de baloncesto, vamos mal", sentencia quien no metió canastas pero que tanto cuidó de quienes sí lo hicieron. Los Gasol, Serge Ibaka, Amaya Valdemoro, Anna Cruz... y Lorena Torres. Campeones 'made in USA'.
