articles.title: Marcelinho Huertas se despide de Tenerife y de la ACB para ir a Dubái: "Es el último desafío de mi carrera"
articles.standfirst: El base de 43 años deja España convertido en leyenda y volverá a jugar en la Euroliga a las órdenes de Xavi Pascual
articles.summary: El base de 43 años deja España convertido en leyenda y volverá a jugar en la Euroliga a las órdenes de Xavi Pascual
articles.body: El base brasileño Marcelinho Huertas abandona La Laguna Tenerife después de siete temporadas para fichar por el Dubai, de la Euroliga, lo que supone no sólo el adiós de un jugador que ha marcado época en el club, sino de una de las figuras más determinantes de la Liga Endesa en su historia reciente. "Creo que hay una llama dentro de mí que sigue moviéndome y es lo que me trajo hasta aquí. Yo me he movido siempre a base de desafíos. Me parece que este desafío es un desafío increíble y creo que es, sinceramente, el último que podría presentarse en mi carrera. Por eso he tomado la decisión de ir a por ello", confesó Huertas en rueda de prensa, visiblemente emocionado. Tras 19 años en España (2003-2026, con un paréntesis de una temporada en Italia y otro de dos en la NBA), el base brasileño deja Tenerife con 43 años y un palmarés con que tardará en igualarse en la isla: una Liga de Campeones, dos Copas Intercontinentales, un subcampeonato en la Copa del Rey y dos terceros puestos en Liga Endesa, además de una larga lista de récords individuales. "Hay momentos para los que nunca estamos del todo preparados. Aunque sepas que llegarán, cuando llegan las palabras se quedan cortas. Hoy me toca vivir una de ellos. Después de siete temporadas, cierro una de las etapas más bonitas de mi vida", afirmó. Acompañado por el presidente del Club Baloncesto Canaria (La Laguna Tenerife en las últimas temporadas), Aniano Cabrera, Huertas explicó que abandonar el equipo a mitad de temporada ha sido una de las decisiones más difíciles de toda su carrera. "Durante estos años surgieron oportunidades difíciles de rechazar, como ha mencionado Aniano, pero siempre encontré motivos para quedarme aquí, porque siempre fui muy feliz, porque me sentía valorado, querido, respetado. Porque sentía que aún nos quedaban cosas por conseguir juntos y porque Tenerife dejó de ser un lugar donde jugaba a baloncesto para convertirse en mi casa", añadió. Ahora se va persiguiendo el desafío de la Euroliga a "otro equipo" cuyo nombre evitó mencionar hoy. En el club dan por sentado que es el Dubai, pero Cabrera sólo reveló que, cuando el agente de Marcelinho le trasladó la oferta que había recibido, únicamente le hizo dos preguntas al jugador: "¿Te atrae la idea? ¿Te hace ilusión?". La respuesta que le dio está implícita en las explicaciones de Huertas de hoy. "Sabiendo quién es Marce y todo lo que nos ha dado, y no voy a enumerar todos los éxitos que hemos logrado con él estos años, me quedo con todas las cosas buenas, por lo que es, lo que ha sido y lo que será para nuestro club", argumentó Cabrera. El internacional brasileño dedicó buena parte de su comparecencia a dirigirse a la afición aurinegra: "Gracias por cuidarme, por confiar en mí, por exigirme, por hacerme sentir parte de algo tan especial. Me siento profundamente orgulloso de haber vivido aquí unos de los mejores años de mi vida como jugador, compitiendo al máximo nivel y con una ilusión que nunca se apagó". ¿Quiere ganar Marcelinho la Euroliga en el tramo final de su carrera? Huertas no esquivó la pregunta ante la prensa que le ha seguido estos años en el pabellón Santiago Martín: "Cada vez que yo entro en una cancha de baloncesto, entro para ganar, para competir y para luchar por lo máximo, sea con la camiseta que sea". ¿Y lo ve posible con 43 años? El brasileño lo tiene claro: "La edad puede ser un condicionante para algunas cosas, pero para otras quizás no. Mi hambre por el baloncesto, por competir, sigue intacta y espero que pueda seguir durante lo que queda", sentenció. Huertas se va convencido de "volver a intentar lo que la gente cree que es imposible". "Pero para mí, es baloncesto", aclaró. Marcelinho Huertas detalló que estos días ha tenido conversaciones que le han resultado "muy duras" -porque eran una despedida- con su entrenador, Jaka Lakovic, y con sus compañeros. "Todos me han dicho lo mismo: 'Mira, tú no tienes que disculparte de nada, tú realmente te lo mereces, te lo has ganado, te vas y punto. Y nosotros seguiremos'. Y yo estoy seguro que seguirán bien y muy bien, porque ya lo han demostrado muchas veces que este equipo es un equipo y no es el equipo de un jugador, y es un equipazo", concluyó.

articles.title: Kansas' Tyran Stokes Talks 'Personal' Kentucky Matchup After Win in Champions Classic
articles.summary: Kansas freshman star Tyran Stokes brought some extra juice into Tuesday night's matchup against Kentucky in the Champions Classic.
articles.body:
Kansas freshman star Tyran Stokes brought some extra juice into Tuesday night's matchup against Kentucky in the Champions Classic.

Before Stokes signed with the Jayhawks, the Wildcats were also a finalist for the Louisville native. So Tuesday's game was especially meaningful for Stokes as he dropped 23 points, 10 rebounds and four assists to lead Kansas to an 89-69 victory.

"I mean, I'm pretty sure everyone obviously knows. For me, it was up to Kansas and Kentucky for my last two schools," Stokes said after the game, per ESPN's Myron Metcalf . "I'm from Louisville. I had a long recruiting process with Kentucky, so obviously when I chose Kansas and I knew that game was going to be here, it was personal for sure. But we got the [win], played together great as a team. That's all that matters."

Bryce James Stats vs. Northern Arizona 🔢

Widely projected as the No. 1 pick in the 2027 NBA draft, Stokes rose to the occasion while playing in front of dozens of NBA scouts and executives in attendance at the United Center. In addition to showcasing his skill set, he also showed poise as he didn't let his emotions get the better of him in the rivalry game.

"For me, just growing up, I was a [North Carolina-Louisville] fan. A lot of my family either likes Louisville or Kentucky, but I was on the Louisville side," Stokes said. "So, growing up, you know the tradition and the rivalry that was between Louisville and Kentucky. So being from Louisville, I still got that same emotion as if I was playing for Louisville. But I'm here in Kansas, so obviously being able to play against a school like that is just one of one and it's my first time to step on a big stage and show what I can do."

Stokes and the Jayhawks (3-0) will have a long layoff before they return to action next Tuesday against UNLV (2-0).

articles.title: Draymond Green Addresses Jordan Poole-Warriors Reunion Comments, 'I'm Not One to Hold Grudges'
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors star forward Draymond Green isn't going to stand in the way of a potential reunion with New Orleans Pelicans guard Jordan Poole.
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors star forward Draymond Green isn't going to stand in the way of a potential reunion with New Orleans Pelicans guard Jordan Poole.

After Poole expressed interest in returning to the Warriors following Monday night's 138-87 blowout win for Golden State, Green was asked about his comments, and he said he would have no problem with playing alongside Poole again.

"We had our issue that I f--ked up on, and that's that," Green told Danny Emerman of the San Francisco Standard on Monday. "But I'm not one to hold grudges, I'm not one to sit around and try to damper something for someone else. So if that's what he wants, I understand that. But that's not a Draymond issue. That's a Golden State Warriors decision."

Dray in Support of Yaxel's Trash Talk 🗣️

Poole was shipped away from the Warriors three seasons ago, a year after he and Green had a physical confrontation during practice. The once-promising sharpshooter has struggled to find consistency away from Golden State, so it's not surprising that he would want to return to where he was at his best.

Green went on to affirm during his podcast that he would stand by the Warriors' decision to bring back Poole if that's what the organization chose to do.

"What those comments were -- they asked me about Jordan Poole's comments … and they were asking me, like, how did I feel about that," he said. "And I told them I don't have a problem with that at all. Number one, I don't make decisions here. I'm a basketball player. I don't decide my own future here, let alone someone else's... Number two, what I said was also, I'm an adult. So if you're asking me as if that's going to be a problem for me, that's no problem for me … I'm not someone who walks around with a grudge."

articles.title: Celtics' Paul George Addresses Jaylen Brown-Jayson Tatum Tension and Drops Honest Quote About 76ers
articles.summary: Boston Celtics star Paul George indicated his focus was more on supporting Jayson Tatum than beating his former teammates in a Tuesday night road game against the Philadelphia 76ers.
articles.body:
Boston Celtics star Paul George indicated his focus was more on supporting Jayson Tatum than beating his former teammates in a Tuesday night road game against the Philadelphia 76ers.

The contest marked George's first game against the Sixers since he was dealt in July as part of the trade for Jaylen Brown, although that storyline did not receive as much attention as the reunion between Tatum and Brown.

"My job was just to come in and support JT, and be the best version that I could be for him," George said when asked Tuesday night if he felt he needed to "make a statement" with so much attention directed toward Tatum and Brown. "That was my only focus."

George continued, "The narrative around it was more than it should have been, and I thought JT handled it perfectly... The biggest thing, before I got here, was the maturity that I saw, and that's, I think, what's separating him."

George racked up a game-high 36 points as the Celtics secured a 123-101 victory over Brown and the 76ers.

Tatum, who contributed 21 points, received what appeared to be a cold reception from Brown both before and after the Celtics victory.

George credited both his health and his deployment by the 76ers as part of the reason he has averaged 22 points through 10 games with the Celtics after contributed 16.7 points per game across two injury-limited seasons with the Sixers.

"What I've learned is, I'm a little bit better with more usage," George said on the postgame broadcast. "And that's no knock to how my opportunities here with Philly— Quite frankly, I wasn't healthy to take on the workload that I feel I'm at my best at.

"Here in Boston, they gave me the opportunity to come out here and play and be myself. Joe [Mazzulla] has integrated me right into the offense and allowed me to just be myself."

The Celtics improved to 9-2 with a Tuesday night win that allowed the team to leapfrog the Sixers and claim the top spot in the Eastern Conference. Brown and his teammates will now look to ride the momentum of their four-game win streak into a Wednesday night matchup at the Toronto Raptors.

articles.title: Darius Acuff Jr. Says He's 'Not a Loser' amid Kings' 1-10 Start to NBA Season
articles.summary: Sacramento Kings rookie Darius Acuff Jr. is unhappy with how the team has performed amid a 1-10 start to the season.
articles.body:
Sacramento Kings rookie Darius Acuff Jr. is unhappy with how the team has performed amid a 1-10 start to the season.

Following the Kings' 107-100 loss to the Orlando Magic on Tuesday, Acuff explained he's "not a loser," and their lack of success thus far is getting to him.

"A lot," Acuff said when asked how much of a toll the losses were taking on him. "I'm not a loser, so it's not fun. But like I said, it's an 82-game season, so hopefully something will stick."

5 Stars Who Could Make First All-NBA Team 🌟

The Kings weren't necessarily expected to be a playoff contender this season after going 22-60 in 2025-26, but even by their usual standards things are in a bad spot right now.

Sacramento's 1-10 record is tied for the worst 11-game start in franchise history. It previously happened during the 1990-91 season. That group did rebound enough to reach 25 wins by the end of the year.

This Kings team hasn't really shown anything to suggest it can win 24 more games. They rank in the bottom five in both offensive and defensive rating. Seven of their 10 losses have been by at least 10 points.

Acuff has also been the subject of criticism because of how many shots he's taking on a nightly basis. His mark of 22.8 field-goal attempts per game is tied for third-most , behind only Anthony Edwards (26.0) and Luka Dončić (24.3).

Despite questions about the dynamic between Acuff and Domantas Sabonis, the two reportedly get along very well, with Sabonis enjoying playing with the rookie as he gets acclimated to the NBA.

The Kings used the No. 7 pick in the 2026 draft on Acuff with the idea he would become their new face of the franchise. His individual performance has been erratic, as is the case for rookies, but he is averaging 26.2 points and 7.3 assists per game through his first 11 starts.

Oscar Robertson is the only rookie in NBA history to average at least 25 points and seven assists per game.

articles.title: Paul George gives 'a**hole' Sixers fan the finger late in Celtics' blowout win
articles.summary: George said his return to Philly after the trade that ended his time as a Sixer felt like "a normal game." But sometimes even normal games can get a little t...
articles.body:
It didn't get nearly as much attention as the fact that Jaylen Brown would be squaring off against the Boston Celtics for the first time in his career, but Tuesday night's matchup with the Philadelphia 76ers also marked Paul George's first trip back to Philly since being dealt to Boston for Brown in the summertime blockbuster that launched a thousand references to beef, lamb chops, gravy and all manner of other comestibles.

It's understandable that George's return didn't resonate as much as the face-off between Brown and Jayson Tatum, given the nine years they spent together in Boston and the unpleasant public falling-out that has come since the trade. George, after all, wasn't a lifer in Philly to nearly the extent that Brown was in Boston.

"Had I been here eight, nine, 10 years, it'd be a different story," George said, according to Adam Himmelsbach of the Boston Globe . "I was here two years. [...] Obviously, it's a tremendous fan base. A great sports town to play in. So that was appreciated. There's no ill will for me. It'll be just fun to compete. Outside of that, it's a normal game."

Sometimes, though, even a normal game can get a little testy.

After drilling his fourth 3-pointer of the night to give the visitors an 18-point lead with just over 9:30 remaining in the fourth quarter, cameras caught George giving something else to one lucky attendee at Xfinity Mobile Arena:

So, Paul: What happened to turn "no ill will for me" into "flipping some guy the bird?"

"There was a fan being an a**hole," George said in the locker room after the game. "[The] ball rolled to him. He looked me dead in my eyes, dropped the ball on the ground as if, like, I'm a dog to go fetch or go get it, instead of passing the ball to me like a normal fan would do. And, so … yeah. So then I rolled him a middle finger in return."

The pointed salute was far from the only portion of screw-you that the six-time All-NBA selection served up on Tuesday:

George ripped off a 14-5 run by himself over a four-minute span in the fourth quarter, turning Tuesday's tilt into a laugher. He'd finish with a game-high 36 points on 14-for-22 shooting, including a 6-for-11 mark from 3-point range, with five rebounds and an assist in 30 minutes of work as the Celtics knocked off the rival Sixers, 123-101 , in a matchup of the top two seeds in the Eastern Conference.

"He took ownership of those fourth-quarter minutes. That's what we needed," Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla said after the game, according to Tara Sullivan of the Boston Globe . "You can't run away from the obvious things that are going on, but he's been traded [three] times, so not the first time he had to go through something like that."

The lights-out performance continued a stellar start to the season for George, who's averaging 22 points, 5.2 rebounds, 3.8 assists, 2.1 steals and 4.9 deflections per game for the Celtics, shooting 49% from the field, 44% from 3-point range and 82% at the free-throw line while playing excellent defense.

George made it clear after the trade that he viewed his role in his new surroundings as complementary — providing support for incumbent superstar Tatum, and doing whatever was necessary to help him elevate the Celtics back into championship contention. He did exactly that on Tuesday, turning what was pitched as a highly emotional contest for Tatum (who finished with 21 points, 6 rebounds and 4 assists) into an evening where the outcome ceased to be in doubt midway through the final frame.

"At this point in my career, there's only one thing I want to do, and that's win," George said during a postgame interview with NBC. "For him, especially, for JT, is to alleviate any pressure, any friction. I'm here to help you. I'm here to serve you, make you become the best player that you can become."

By playing like he has to start the season, helping the Celtics to a 9-2 record with top-five units on both offense and defense , George isn't just alleviating pressure on Tatum. He's also applying plenty of it to the opposition, ensuring that Boston hasn't skipped a beat since that massive summertime trade … and leaving opposing fans muttering some of the same curses under their breath that George preferred to communicate digitally on Tuesday.

articles.title: Warriors' Yaxel Lendeborg Says Draymond Green Was 'Encouraging' Trash Talk vs. Luka Doncic, Lakers
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors forward Yaxel Lendeborg made waves with his comments about Los Angeles Lakers superstar guard Luka Dončić last month, and the rookie revealed this week that his actions may have been egged on by a teammate.
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors forward Yaxel Lendeborg made waves with his comments about Los Angeles Lakers superstar guard Luka Dončić last month, and the rookie revealed this week that his actions may have been egged on by a teammate.

In an interview with Nick Friedell of The Athletic, Lendeborg suggested that veteran teammate Draymond Green was the one who inspired him to speak his mind.

"He was encouraging that," Lendeborg said. "Draymond likes all that, because there was no reason for me to back down to anybody. We're both in the same league. Regardless of what [Dončić has] done, he hasn't done it to me. So [Draymond] was basically going off, if he hasn't proven it to you, then why should you be backing down and scared of him?

"I don't care what you did, if you scored 70 points on [someone else]—you didn't score 70 on me. So that's the kind of the mindset he told me to get into. And he's such a huge competitor as well, so having him in my back as well, leaning on me towards that situation was great for me."

Following the Warriors' 127-105, season-opening loss to the Lakers, Lendeborg didn't mince words regarding his feelings about Dončić.

At the time, Lendeborg told reporters , "I had a lot of respect for him [because] I didn't really watch the NBA much. I just watched highlights and seen him kill people. But being in it firsthand and seeing all the whining and complaining, I lost all respect."

Dončić had a game-high 28 points in the Lakers' victory, while Lendeborg finished with 12 points in his NBA debut.

That marked the first of three losses to open the season for the Warriors, but they have since bounced back in a big way with eight straight victories, including one over the Lakers.

Lendeborg has been a huge part of Golden State's early-season success as well, ranking second on the team with 21.4 points per game.

With his play speaking for itself and Green endorsing his attitude, Lendeborg is trending toward becoming a legitimate star for a Warriors team that is looking like a potential Western Conference contender.

articles.title: Jaylen Brown Praises Jayson Tatum After 76ers' Loss to Celtics in 1st Game vs. Ex-Teammate
articles.summary: Despite losing his first meeting against his former Boston Celtics team on Tuesday night, Philadelphia 76ers star guard Jaylen Brown mustered up some kind words about ex-teammate Jayson Tatum.
articles.body:
Despite losing his first meeting against his former Boston Celtics team on Tuesday night, Philadelphia 76ers star guard Jaylen Brown mustered up some kind words about ex-teammate Jayson Tatum.

"I'm just focused on doing what's best for my team," Brown said after the Sixers' 123-101 loss, per ESPN's Kris Rhim . "Everything else was just, to be honest, I wasn't paying attention, but credit to Jayson; he played well tonight."

Brown and Tatum's first meeting as opponents kicked off with an icy exchange in which Brown ignored his former teammate's pregame greeting.

From there, Brown struggled to find his footing, finishing with 13 points in the loss. Tatum scored 21 for the Celtics, who were led by Paul George's 36-point explosion.

Brown and Tatum won't meet on the court again until January, so they can put the hubbub about their relationship behind them as they move forward with their respective teams.

articles.title: Inside the numbers: Blowouts are common, close games rare so far in this NBA season
articles.summary: MIAMI (AP) — The blowouts keep coming in the NBA, like never before.Entering Wednesday, with 13% of the season played, the average winning margin in the NBA...
articles.body:
MIAMI (AP) — The blowouts keep coming in the NBA, like never before.

Entering Wednesday, with 13% of the season played, the average winning margin in the NBA has been 13.8 points per game. It's the most lopsided start to a season in league history; the average margin through the comparative point in the 1949-50 season was 13.4 points per game.

At this rate, the NBA would set a victory-margin record for a fourth consecutive season. And so far, the league has seen more games decided by 30 or more points (15) than it has games decided by three points or less (13).

"We got our (butt) kicked. No other way to put it," New Orleans coach Jamahl Mosley said earlier this week after the Pelicans lost by 51 points earlier this week to Golden State — the biggest blowout in the league so far this season. "They came in and punched us in the mouth."

This will be no consolation to Mosley, but there's a lot of that going around.

Chicago enters Wednesday being outscored by 16.7 points per game, which would be the worst margin in league history (though, in fairness, it is way too early to declare that mark in jeopardy). Dallas, in 1992-93, was outscored by 15.2 points per game for the league-worst mark.

Charlotte has already lost three games by at least 33 points this season; the Hornets didn't have even one such loss last season.

Milwaukee is getting outscored by nearly 15 points per game, with three losses of 25 or more.

"It's part of our journey," Milwaukee coach Taylor Jenkins said. "It's our opportunity. Not going to call it a challenge; it's an opportunity. I think we've got a lot of guys that have got to continue to try different things. What we're doing right now is not working."

The flip side to there being so many blowouts is that there have been few close games.

The 13 games decided by three points or less is the fewest at this point in a season in 60 years. There were 25 such games at this point last season, 38 such games at this point in 2024-25.

Almost half the league — 14 of the 30 teams — has yet to have a game end with a margin of three points or less this season. Atlanta is 2-0 in those games; no other team has won more than one. New Orleans (1-2) and Brooklyn (0-2) are the only teams to lose more than one of those contests to this point.

Michael Jordan never did it. Kobe Bryant and Kareem Abdul-Jabbar never did either. LeBron James and Kevin Durant also haven't pulled it off.

Elite scorers, all of them, but they never averaged a point per minute for a full season.

And that's another layer of what makes the flying starts for the NBA's three leading scorers so far this season — the Los Angeles Lakers' Luka Doncic, Golden State's Stephen Curry and San Antonio's Victor Wembanyama — even more impressive.

They're scoring a ton, and they're doing it quickly. Very quickly.

"There's a lot of good going on," Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said after Wembanyama had a 40-point effort — along with 11 rebounds and nine blocked shots — in just 25 minutes of a win over Phoenix earlier this week.

The Lakers, Warriors and Spurs all play Wednesday night, and it's still early enough in the season where one "off" night can skew numbers considerably. But Doncic, Curry and Wembanyama got through the first three weeks of the season averaging more than 1 point per minute. That's a pace almost unheard of in NBA history.

Among players with at least 1,500 points in a season, only one player has pulled off the point-per-minute feat: Wilt Chamberlain in 1961-62, his 50.4-point-per-game year.

Chamberlain was at 1.04 points per minute that season, while logging an average — yes, an average — of more than 48 minutes per game, thanks to overtimes. He was off the floor for a total of eight minutes that season in Philadelphia's 80 games; an ejection in the fourth quarter of a game against the Los Angeles Lakers on Jan. 3, 1962 marked his only off-court stint all season.

Entering Wednesday, Wembanyama is averaging 1.01 points per minute, Doncic is at 1.09 and Curry is at 1.07.

"He's one of one," Warriors coach Steve Kerr said of Curry — who enters Wednesday with six straight games of at least one point per minute.

articles.title: Houston Comets president shares which WNBA player would be the ‘ultimate dream’
articles.summary: Jennifer Rizzotti is looking ahead to the Houston Comets’ return to the WNBA. The Houston Comets are at a turning point right now as they get ready to step b...
articles.body:
Jennifer Rizzotti is looking ahead to the Houston Comets' return to the WNBA.

The Houston Comets are at a turning point right now as they get ready to step back onto the WNBA court. Coming off the relocation of the Connecticut Sun franchise, the team finds itself right in the middle of the draft lottery following a tough 2026 season.

But there's plenty of reason for optimism, as Houston is tied for the top odds at 32.9% to land the No. 1 overall pick. Thanks to the lottery rules, they can't drop past third, giving them a real shot to draft a superstar and kick off this new chapter right away.

Jennifer Rizzotti would love a player like A'ja Wilson

Speaking on the team's mindset, Houston Comets President Jennifer Rizzotti laid out exactly what she wants in their next draft pick. For her, she wants someone like A'ja Wilson , who brings an unmatched work ethic and leadership that can reshape an entire franchise from day one.

"You know, obviously, you know, when you look at like who's done it the best, you've got to look at A'ja Wilson, right? And we, you know, we can't all get A'ja Wilsons, but you hope that you'll continue to have players like her. They're—they're great when they come out of college already.

"However, they have a work ethic that will, you know, supersede just talent, right? So she wanted to not just be the best coming out of college, but she wanted to be the best period. And then you add on top of it her leadership, right? You watch how she talks to her teammates, how she treats her teammates, how much they respect her, and how they play for her.

"Like, that's like the ultimate dream if you can get a player like A'ja Wilson into your organization. They don't grow on trees, though, right? So, so then for us, like, we, you know, we're hoping to have a pretty high draft pick because we're in the lottery."

A'ja Wilson has solidified her spot among the all-time greats, bringing home a record-extending fifth WNBA MVP, her third in a row. She put together a crazy season, leading the league with 26.2 points per game and becoming the first player ever to post back-to-back 1,000-point years.

Beyond the numbers, her relentless drive and locker-room leadership are why she's the absolute gold standard for what a WNBA superstar looks like today.

articles.title: Celtics Have Found a Simple Way to Make Even the Best Defenses Look Silly
articles.summary: Teams are having a hard time keeping up with one of Boston's favorite actions.
articles.body:
It's been a promising start to the season for the Boston Celtics .

After taking down the Philadelphia 76ers, the Celtics now own the best record in the Eastern Conference. They also own the best net rating in the NBA, outscoring opponents by a whopping 12.4 points per 100 possessions .

The Celtics are getting it done on both ends of the court, ranking third in both offensive efficiency and defensive efficiency .

One reason the Celtics have been so dominant offensively is their use of flare screens.

A flare screen is when a player sets a screen for a teammate moving away from the ball, typically toward the perimeter.

Derrick White has the ball on the right wing while Neemias Queta sets a screen to free Paul George for a cut toward the left wing.

Because Queta isn't a major perimeter scoring threat, his defender, Joel Embiid, can sag off him to provide help elsewhere.

The problem? When George's defender, VJ Edgecombe, gets caught up on Queta's screen, that leaves George wide open on the 3-point line.

You can probably guess how this particular possession ended.

First and foremost, Queta is setting a ton of flare screens this season.

On Nov. 9, NBA analyst Nekias Duncan shared that Queta had set 59 flare screens through the first 10 games of the season, which was more than all but eight teams.

Secondly, it's a really smart way to use George.

George has been particularly effective in those situations this season. According to NBA.com , he's averaging 1.88 points per possession, which is by far the best rate in the NBA.

That efficiency isn't sustainable over an entire season, but George has long been one of the NBA's better off-screen scorers. He's an excellent shooter who knows how to use screens to create separation and get his shot off quickly.

Thirdly, it's a great way to put opposing defenses in a difficult position.

If the defense focuses too much on taking away the 3-pointer, they risk giving up easy layups or dunks.

"Boston is one of the best teams in the league off the ball," Chicago Bulls head coach Tiago Splitter said . "It's impressive how they play all those flare situations. It's really difficult to be aware of the flares that are coming."

With George, Jayson Tatum, Derrick White and several other capable shooters, the Celtics have no shortage of players who can capitalize when a defender gets caught on a screen. And with Queta doing so much of the dirty work, the Celtics have found another way to make their already dangerous offense even less predictable.

articles.title: Kevin Garnett Explains Why He's 'So Disappointed' in Bam Adebayo, Evan Mobley, Paolo Banchero
articles.summary: Hall of Famer Kevin Garnett is "so disappointed" by the lack of development he sees in some of the NBA's brightest young forwards.
articles.body:
Hall of Famer Kevin Garnett is "so disappointed" by the lack of development he sees in some of the NBA's brightest young forwards.

In the first episode of his new show with ESPN's Stephen A. Smith, Garnett cited the Miami Heat's Bam Adebayo, Cleveland Cavaliers' Evan Mobley and Orlando Magic's Paolo Banchero as three players whom he doesn't think are fulfilling their potential.

"I used Bam because I love watching him. I love his style, but I'm also watching the league of young guys," the retired NBA star said (2:21:57 mark). "I'm watching Mobley. I'm watching Bam. I'm watching all the younger guys. And each time I watch [Adebayo], I see him with guys that never played in the league. But I sit and I go, 'I want to see what Bam brought this year that's gonna make him one of the best bigs this year. I want to see what Evan Mobley gonna bring this year. I want to see what Paolo gonna bring.'

"So I'm sitting here just articulating the league, and I get so disappointed when I go away with what I'm expecting to see versus what I'm looking at. Then that tells me you did nothing in the summer."

Mobley in particular drew some Garnett comparisons coming out of the draft because of his lanky 6'11" frame. He was an elite defender by his second season, and the hope was that he'd develop the scoring prowess to go along with that.

Mobley's game simply hasn't grown to that point. Especially in the playoffs, he hasn't emerged as a star who can carry an offense.

It's a similar story with Adebayo. His 83-point outburst aside, he hasn't evolved to where he can be the No. 1 option on a title contender. That much was clear last year as Miami didn't make the playoffs.

Banchero, meanwhile, exceeded expectations as a rookie but seems to have plateaued. The talent is obviously there, yet something is just missing . He doesn't attack the rim like a 6'10" forward should, and he's not an efficient enough shooter to justify his shot selection.

Garnett's general criticism may sound harsh, but he's mostly echoing what people who follow the NBA have said already.

Adebayo, Banchero and Mobley are all former All-Stars and very good players. In the case of all three, there may not be a lot of fans who feel they've hit their full ceiling.

articles.title: Lauri Markkanen Injured, Latest News on Jazz Star's Timeline to Return After Hand Fracture
articles.summary: The Utah Jazz will spend the near next four weeks without Lauri Markkanen after already losing Jusuf Nurkić and Jaren Jackson Jr. to injury.
articles.body:
The Utah Jazz will spend the near next four weeks without Lauri Markkanen after already losing Jusuf Nurkić and Jaren Jackson Jr. to injury.

Markkanen will be sidelined for at least a month after suffering two non-displaced fractures in his right hand, the Jazz announced Wednesday.

ESPN's Shams Charania and Tim MacMahon first reported the news on Wednesday.

Markkanen has already sat out two games since he last played Friday at the Dallas Mavericks.

The Jazz currently sit in the basement of the Western Conference after a 1-10 start to the 2026-27 campaign.

Markkanen had ranked second in the team scoring race with 18 points per game to go along with 6.8 rebounds and two assists through eight contests.

His injury issues started Oct. 26 when he left a matchup against the visiting Memphis Grizzlies early with a right wrist injury .

Markkanen sat out one contest, then returned to play a four-game stretch capped off by scoring 24 points in 34 minutes during Friday's game against the Mavericks.

Two days later, Markkanen was ruled out of Sunday's matchup at the Minnesota Timberwolves with what the team described as a right wrist sprain .

KSL's Chandler Holt reported Markkanen's latest injury believed to be is "unrelated" to the wrist issue other than taking place in the same arm.

Markkanen's extended absence comes as the latest blow to a Jazz roster already missing Nurkić, Jackson and Keyonte George to injury.

Nurkić suffered an injury to the second toe of his right foot during the preseason and is next set to be re-evaluated around Nov. 20, according to the Jazz .

Jaren Jackson Jr. suffered a torn MCL in his right knee on Oct. 26 and is facing an estimated six- to eight-week recovery timeline that would place his potential return around mid-December, per MacMahon and Charania .

George, the Jazz's leading scorer so far this season, missed his team's last game with what Utah described as a right ankle sprain.

Jazz governor Ryan Smith said in an appearance on KSL Sports' Scotty G. & The Coach last weekend he had faith in coach Will Hardy as well as CEO Danny Ainge and president of basketball operations Austin Ainge.

Losing Markkanen, Nurkić and Jackson on a long-term basis will make it significantly more difficult for Hardy and the Jazz executives to reward that faith with a competitive season.

The Jazz will for now hope to get positive injury news about George so the third-year guard can join Darryn Peterson and Ace Bailey in leading their team for at least the next few weeks.

articles.title: How the Jayson Tatum-Jaylen Brown beef turned a November game into an NBA Finals-esque atmosphere
articles.summary: Beef is back on the menu in the NBA.
articles.body: Beef is back on the menu in the NBA. It’s rare for a November game to feel like a Game 7 playoff tilt, but Tuesday night’s showdown in Philadelphia between the 76ers and Boston Celtics certainly delivered that kind of electric atmosphere in spades. The first meeting between Jaylen Brown’s 76ers and Jayson Tatum’s Boston Celtics was the first time the former teammates would square off since Brown was sent packing from Beantown over the summer. It was the kind of interpersonal drama that takes an entire writers room of reality television producers to conjure up. After being teammates for nine years, Brown was shopped around the league by the Boston front office before eventually being dealt to Philadelphia in exchange for Paul George and four draft picks. The former University of California star had very obviously blamed Tatum for forcing him out of Boston, even as Tatum claimed ignorance of the efforts to trade Brown until the moment it happened. An ensuing back-and-forth through the press and on social media – sometimes in emoji form – escalated things in the weeks leading up to the game. That sniping through the press and on Instagram made it the most anticipated coming together of former teammates since Kevin Durant signed with the Golden Warriors and went back to Oklahoma City to face Russell Westbrook and the Thunder. And while the game ended up being a blowout – Boston went on a huge run at the end of the third quarter and into the fourth quarter to win 123-101 – the real excitement came in the moments before tipoff. As Brown spun the game ball on his finger before tip, Tatum approached. The ensuing interaction was … icy. It was emblematic of the whole beef between these two, as Tatum has repeatedly attempted to take the high road while Brown has made his antipathy for the Celtics star known. Tatum said in a podcast that he was caught off guard by the trade that sent Brown to Philly, and when that clip was posted to Instagram, Brown left a comment with a cap emoji (his way of calling Tatum a liar). When asked about Brown’s comment, Tatum said “there’s no beef” between the pair that played together in Boston for nine years. In reply, Brown agreed there was no beef but “it might be a little bit of lamb chops and gravy,” added that Tatum had a great public relations team and cryptically said the former Duke star should “stay ready at all times.” It’s still not really clear what sparked Brown’s departure from Boston. He played Robin to Tatum’s Batman for many years before Tatum’s Achilles injury in 2025 knocked him out for most of last season. That allowed Brown to take center stage in Beantown and it’s possible that he was done being the secondary star to Tatum. There have been lots of other rumblings out of Boston – that Brown was moody and a difficult personality, that Tatum felt challenged and wanted him out – that no one has ever gone on the record to confirm. Brown and Tatum both downplayed the moment and their less-than-joyful meetup. “I’m just focused on getting out and doing what’s best for my team … to be honest, I wasn’t paying attention, but, you know, credit to Jason, he played well tonight,” a frustrated Brown said when asked about the moment. He downplayed the idea of having more emotion for the game, which was derailed for him by early foul trouble, but admitted, “I was looking forward to this, I was looking forward to playing well but sh*t happens.” “No headlines about anything like that,” Tatum said of the moment between him and Brown. “I was just getting ready for the game, ready for jump ball, go out there, compete, have some fun, and try to get a win.” Still, Tatum told reporters the game felt like an NBA Finals game. And that’s the point – beef is good. The NBA Playoffs are a remarkable exhibition of athletic competition, but the league’s regular season is often just a monthslong bit of positioning for that springtime push. It often seems to only exist for The Discourse: Is load management good? Who’s going to get traded? Who’s going to win MVP? What teams are obviously tanking? Those questions drive the conversation; the games themselves don’t matter a ton until the calendar turns to March and April. But when there are real rivalries and real drama playing out on the court – such as what happened with Tatum and Brown, even though both tried to move on afterward – then the games really matter. That’s how you get a crowd in the City of Brotherly Love to treat an early season game like it was a title-clincher. Both teams brought it in that vein until – like any good bit of reality TV – the main storyline was turned on its head by an unexpected participant. The real winner of the night was George, the man often forgotten in the trade drama. The 36-year-old went off for 36 points and helped put the finishing touches on the massive run in the third and fourth quarters that put the kibosh on the 76ers’ attempt to get back in the game.

articles.title: Steph Curry goes off on former NBA players for criticizing Ayesha Curry
articles.summary: Stephen Curry is calling out former NBA players Nick Young, Gilbert Arenas and others after comments about his wife, Ayesha.
articles.body:
Stephen Curry has made it clear that he is not pleased with the criticism directed at his wife, Ayesha Curry, following the release of her new movie. The Golden State Warriors superstar addressed the growing conversation involving former NBA players Nick Young and Gilbert Arenas, along with former NFL player Emmanuel Acho and others who have shared their opinions about her.

The controversy began after Ayesha appeared in the Roku romantic comedy "Second Chance Holiday," which features an on-screen kissing scene with co-star Matthew Daddario. The scene attracted criticism from several sports personalities, with LeSean McCoy questioning her decision to participate in it.

Arenas also took aim at Ayesha during an appearance on the We Said What We Said podcast with Young, calling her the only blemish in Stephen's family and arguing that she does not behave like other NBA stars' wives.

Steph Curry tells critics to keep Ayesha's name out of their mouths

Stephen addressed the criticism in a video, explaining that the conversation had gone beyond the usual noise surrounding his family.

"I've been hearing a lot of noise, and usually the noise doesn't bother me or Ayesha," Curry said. "But this one in particular, when people are trying to step on the accomplishments of my wife, leading podcasts and giving opinions on somebody else's wife, I don't know why Nick, Gil, Emmanuel and anybody else feel the need to jump in and give an opinion on something they don't really know about."

The Warriors star also suggested the comments revealed a bigger issue with how some people view women and what they believe women should be allowed to do.

Curry made his message particularly clear when addressing those who continue to use Ayesha's name in their headlines.

"Anytime Ayesha Curry shows up in your headline, I'd kindly suggest you give the happy hands, the congratulations and, maybe, an apology as loud as you lead your shows with this topic," he said.

He ended by thanking the critics for the free publicity.

Ayesha Curry stars alongside Matthew Daddario in Second Chance Holiday

Ayesha's latest project premiered on Nov. 5 on The Roku Channel and is her first leading role in a feature film.

Ayesha plays Chelsey, a dating expert who believes she is cursed after repeatedly getting dumped during the holiday season. However, her outlook changes when she reconnects with her high school flame, played by Daddario, and begins to wonder whether her bad luck could lead her back to her first love.

articles.title: Stephen Curry Calls Out Gilbert Arenas, Nick Young in Video After Criticism of Wife Ayesha
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry called out former teammate Nick Young and former NBA star Gilbert Arenas regarding criticism of his wife, Ayesha.
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry called out former teammate Nick Young and former NBA star Gilbert Arenas regarding criticism of his wife, Ayesha.

"Nick, Gil, Emmanuel and anybody else who feels the need to jump in and give an opinion on something you don't really know about, something that kind of speaks to a bigger conversation on how you view women in this world and what they're allowed and what they're not allowed to do," Curry said in a video posted on Instagram (0:24 mark). "Given the ignorance around how acting works, obviously I tried to laugh this one off but something needs to be said. Anytime Ayesha Curry shows up in your headline, kindly suggest that you just give the happy hands, the congratulations, and maybe the apology can be as loud as when y'all leading y'all shows with this topic."

Dray in Support of Yaxel's Trash Talk 🗣️

Arenas and Young previously discussed Ayesha continuing her acting career in the new holiday romance film Second Chance Holiday .

"The only blemish in the family is the wife, in a sense," Arenas said Saturday on the We Said What We Said show (5:30 mark). "Because she doesn't act like the other superstars wives."

"We don't want to hear you," he added. "We just want to know you're there, you're fine. You're taking the pictures, but we don't want to know you."

They eventually apologized for their comments on Wednesday.

"I'm sorry, Steph," Young said on Gil's Arena (0:50 mark). "You my dog. I love you. If I said anything, I apologize like a man. I'm sorry."

"I'm sorry if he's offended, I didn't mean it like that," Arenas added. "I was just saying he's such a perfect dude that you know, but I am sorry."

Ayesha started acting as a teenager and has continued to appear in television shows and movies since getting married to Stephen in 2011. She's also had roles in other Christmas films including Joy to the World and Irish Wish .

Stephen celebrated his wife's latest movie when it was first announced on Oct. 27.

"My Leading Lady," Curry wrote in a post on X. "I get to see the work behind the scenes and now the world gets to see you shine and this is just the beginning…"

Curry was previously teammates with Young during the 2017-18 season, as they won a championship together on the Warriors.

While the two-time MVP never played alongside Arenas, their NBA careers overlapped for three seasons from 2009-12.

Curry has thrived to open his 2026-27 campaign in Golden State, averaging 30.6 points and 4.3 assists per game while shooting 50.3 percent from the field and 45.7 percent from three-point territory.

articles.title: Cleveland Cavaliers vs. New York Knicks Live NBA Updates, Scores and Highlights
articles.summary: The New York Knicks play host to the Cleveland Cavaliers on Wednesday night in what will be the second Eastern Conference Finals rematch of the season.
articles.body:
The New York Knicks play host to the Cleveland Cavaliers on Wednesday night in what will be the second Eastern Conference Finals rematch of the season.

Last time, the reigning NBA champs took care of business rather easily. And they are rolling overall. The Knicks enter having won four straight and six of their last seven.

Cleveland, meanwhile, is struggling to find its footing. The Cavs have lost four of their last five, the most recent of which was a meltdown against the reeling Charlotte Hornets.

Will the Knicks stay hot or will the Cavs climb out of this mini rut? Follow all the latest updates, highlights, analysis and takeaways from this one below!

Or as the kids would say: KAT IS TOO TUFF .

Karl-Anthony Towns has opened up the second quarter with excellent energy. He's attacking on offense, moving on defense and continuing to throw bodies around near the glass.

KAT is now up to 10 points in just 11 minutes. The Knicks are within two as a result.

Score: Cavs 34, Knicks 32 | 9:24 remaining in the second quarter

This won't have any impact on how many people plug Mikal Bridges into their preferred trade machine. Nope, nope, nope, certainly not.

Grown Adult Finish by Karl-Anthony Towns

Kudos for Karl-Anthony Towns' power when turning a corner, but the Cavs defense parted like the Red Sea for him on this one.

Cavs Take a 10-Point Lead into the Second Quarter

Cleveland built the lead with a good amount of shot-making off the bench. Meleek Thomas and Tyrese proctor combined for 13 points, and the Cavs as a team are shooting 69-plus percent inside the arc.

Score: Cavs 33, Knicks 33 | End of the first quarter

Meleek Thomas has been hitting shots like this all season. How did he slip all the way to No. 34?!

Score: Cavs 25, Knicks 16 | 1:51 remaining in the first quarter

Spida didn't incorporate his high pickup dribble into this one, but we'll let that slide.

The Cavs Need More of This From Peyton Watson

Peyton Watson has looked as advertised on defense a lot of the time this season. But his sub-25 percent clip from three isn't going to cut it in this offense.

Especially if James Harden really is entering his washed era.

Score: Cavs 10, Knicks 9 | 6:31 remaining in the first quarter

We are officially off, and Josh Hart may have already re-aggravated his right ankle injury. New York isn't taking him out, though, so maybe he's just getting his sea legs back.

Score: Cavs 4, Knicks 4 | 9:13 remaining in the first quarter

The Knicks are (Sort of) Adding a Former Top-10 Pick

Rob Dillingham has not shown much since being drafted eighth overall in 2024. But he can be shifty on the rock, and in the absence of a second primary ball-handler, the Knicks like to have a bunch of competent secondary decision-makers.

Viewed through this lens, getting Dillingham into the same program that has helped reboot Landry Shamet's career and continued developing Tyler Kolek is a solid flier.

Here's more evidence that Charles Barkley is right.

You can make the case that Evan Mobley spends a lot of time playing away from the basket. But it doesn't really excuse the returns when you look at how other teams with perimeter-oriented bigs still crash the offensive glass.

Cleveland, in fact, is playing one of them tonight. The Knicks remain the NBA's best offensive rebounding squad despite losing Mitchell Robinson to the Boston Celtics and having Karl-Anthony Towns run offensive sets from above the free-throw line.

Charles Barkley Has a Point About the Cavs

Despite having both Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen, the Cavs rank in the bottom 10 of both offensive and defensive rebounding rate.

Granted, Allen's absence has skewed these returns. But Cleveland is still a below-average team on the defensive glass with both bigs on the floor and rates in the 3rd percentile of offensive rebounding to boot.

Having your usual starters isn't typically a big deal. But because of injuries to Peyton Watson and Jarrett Allen, this is just the second time since Halloween Cleveland's preferred fivesome will be available.

Do we think they realize this guy also plays basketball, too?

After missing two games with an ankle injury then one more with an illness, Josh Hart returns to the Knicks' rotation. With Karl-Anthony Towns also getting the green light, this allows New York to roll with its usual starting five of Hart, KAT, Jalen Brunson, Mikal Bridges and OG Anunoby.

articles.title: El Baskonia lo estropea en un último cuarto esperpéntico
articles.standfirst: Compitió tres cuartos ante el Partizan pero acabó sucumbiendo con un parcial de 15-6
articles.summary: Compitió tres cuartos ante el Partizan pero acabó sucumbiendo con un parcial de 15-6
articles.body: El Kosner Baskonia se quedó sin ideas al final del partido ante el Partizan de Belgrado en el que cayó, 80-66, en un esperpéntico último cuarto (15-6) en el que tiró por la borda el buen trabajo que había hecho hasta ese momento El equipo de Perasovic se colocó a sólo un punto (61-60) a un minuto para el final del tercer acto y un parcial de 19-6 en esos últimos 11 minutos de juego acabaron con las opciones de un equipo que sigue hundido en la clasificación con un sólo triunfo en 10 partidos, lo que ya es el peor arranque de competición de los vitorianos con esos partidos jugados. Y eso que el día pintaba muy bien para la reconstrucción de su plantilla. Por la mañana se confirmaba el fichaje de Roland Smits; por la tarde la cesión de Kenan Kamenjas y por la noche el regreso de Rodions Kurucs después de tres semanas de ausencia. Y la presencia del letón en pista se notó mucho. De hecho Kurucs acabó con 10 puntos y 5 rebotes, segundo mejor anotador del equipo, y sobre todo impregnando al equipo de esa intensidad y sacrificio que pone en cada acción. Kurucs y Duarte (15 puntos), mantuvieron a flote al Baskonia los tres primeros cuartos incluso cuando el Partizan amenazaba con romper el partido, como con el 52-42 a 6:10 para el final del tercer acto. El Partizan fue mejor que el Baskonia en el juego interior, con un enorme Jekiri autor de 17 puntos con 8/10 en tiros de campo, y en el control del partido que estuvo en casi todo momento en las manos de Carlik Jones, 16 puntos. Y cuando no estaba Jones, apareció Pajola para gopear a los vitorianos con dos triples en el último cuarto en la construcción de ese demoledor parcial que decidió el partido. En esos infames 11 últimos minutos, el Baskonia sólo anotó una canasta en juego (triple de Duarte) y tres tiros libres de Kurucs. Llegaron a fallar 11 tiros de campo (seis tiros de dos y cinco tiros de tres), y cometieron seis de las 17 pérdidas de todo el partido. Con las incorporaciones y el regreso de Kurucs, el Baskonia empieza a tener mimbres para poder ir a la guerra en la Euroliga con suficentes armas. Ante el Partizan, el equipo compitió y por momentos jugó mejor, pero se quedó sin gasolina al final para caer por décima vez en 11 partidos. Y el problema es que en este tiempo en que se ha ido recomponiendo la plantilla con respecto al equipo del inicio de la temporada, el Baskonia se ha podido quedar muy pronto fuera de las cuentas de la Euroliga. 80 - Partizan Mozzart Belgrade (23+19+23+15): Carlik Jones (16), Ethan Thompson (4), Robert Franks (7), Vanja Marinkovic (6) y Tonye Jekiri (17) -cinco inicial-, Luca Vildoza (2), Nikola Tanaskovic (14), Antonio Reeves (-), Arijan Lakic (5) y Alessandro Pajola (9). 66 - Kosner Baskonia (18+20+22+6): Kobi Simmons (5), DJ Stewart (6), Chris Duarte (15), Stefan Joksimovic (2) y Clement Frisch (8) -cinco inicial-, A.J. articles.title: New Devin Booker Trade Rumors Update Suns Future, Team-Building Plans Ahead of NBA Deadline
articles.summary: Devin Booker isn't interested in parting ways with the Phoenix Suns as the team looks to continue building around him on the trade market, according to HoopsHype's Michael Scotto.
articles.body:
Devin Booker isn't interested in parting ways with the Phoenix Suns as the team looks to continue building around him on the trade market, according to HoopsHype's Michael Scotto.

"From every indication I've gotten, the Phoenix Suns want to keep Devin Booker and they want to continue to build around him and make the team better around him," Scotto reported reported Wednesday on the Deals and Dunks show. "And for Devin Booker, every indication I've gotten is he still wants to be a Sun for life, ideally."

Booker has spent all 12 years of his NBA career on the Suns since they selected him with a first-round pick in the 2015 draft.

He's blossomed into an elite scorer in Phoenix, racking up five All-Star nods and two All-NBA selections. Booker has helped the Suns go on several playoff runs, including an NBA Finals appearance in 2021.

The 30-year-old has repeatedly expressed his desire to retire with Phoenix as well.

Still, the Suns' last two playoff appearances have ended in the first round. They've also struggled to begin this season, sitting at just 4-6 through 10 games.

Phoenix has experienced issues with slowing down opposing offenses, as its 119.3 defensive rating ranks No. 28 in the league (via NBA.com ).

Booker has remained effective despite the slow start by the Suns, averaging 25.1 points, 4.8 assists and 2.7 rebounds per game while compiling 48.3/35.7/93.7 shooting splits.

While front offices around the NBA may inquire about Booker's availability if Phoenix can't get on track before the trade deadline, it doesn't appear as though a change of scenery is on the horizon.

articles.title: Tyrese Haliburton Injury, Return Timeline Updated By Pacers' Rick Carlisle Amid Hamstring Issue
articles.summary: Indiana Pacers head coach Rick Carlisle offered an update on star point guard Tyrese Haliburton on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Indiana Pacers head coach Rick Carlisle offered an update on star point guard Tyrese Haliburton on Wednesday.

Haliburton has been out since Oct. 26 because of a left hamstring strain .

"He's progressing," Carlisle told reporters. "Hamstring is doing better."

Haliburton missed all of last season because of a torn Achilles and hoped to avoid any injuries during the 2026-27 campaign, but just four games into the year, he went down with an ailment.

Before the injury, Haliburton was putting up 21.8 points, 9.5 assists and 4.5 rebounds per game.

The initial timeline for Haliburton's hamstring strain was at least two weeks, and it appears he'll be gone for even longer than that after Carlisle's update on Wednesday.

Indiana has had a rough start to the season, going 3-8 through its first 11 games, and Haliburton's absence will only make things more difficult. Assuming he's set to miss the next 10 days, Haliburton will be absent for a stretch that includes games against the New York Knicks, Philadelphia 76ers and Cleveland Cavaliers.

Should Haliburton be able to return after 10 days, his first game back will be a road contest against the Knicks on Nov. 11.

In the meantime, the Pacers will try to stay afloat without their star.

Andrew Nembhard and Braden Smith have balanced starting point guard duties, with T.J. McConnell and Quenton Jackson coming off the bench. That has led to a strong start for Nembhard in particular, who is putting up 17.1 points and 7.6 assists per game.

articles.title: Thunder Hit With Another Major Injury Blow Ahead of Blazers Rematch
articles.summary: The Thunder suffer another major setback ahead of their Blazers rematch, leaving Shai Gilgeous-Alexander with an even tougher challenge. The post Thunder Hit...
articles.body:
The Oklahoma City Thunder were already running short on healthy bodies. Now, they're losing another key contributor.

Ajay Mitchell has been ruled out of Wednesday's rematch against the Portland Trail Blazers because of a left ankle sprain, according to the NBA's official 4:15 p.m. ET injury report.

The setback comes one night after Oklahoma City suffered a 123-103 loss to Portland, ending its four-game winning streak.

Mitchell's absence leaves coach Mark Daigneault without his second-leading scorer as the Thunder attempt to avoid consecutive losses to the same opponent.

Oklahoma City enters Wednesday at 8-3, but its growing injury list threatens to complicate an otherwise promising start.

Ajay Mitchell Ruled Out After Strong Start to Season

Mitchell has emerged as one of Oklahoma City's most important offensive contributors.

The third-year guard is averaging 18.5 points, 3.6 rebounds and 3.3 assists through 11 games, providing valuable scoring alongside Shai Gilgeous-Alexander .

Mitchell scored 14 points on 6-of-10 shooting in Tuesday's loss to Portland. He also added three rebounds, three assists and a steal in 28 minutes.

His latest injury interrupts an impressive stretch that included one of the best performances of his young career.

Mitchell erupted for a season-high 35 points in Friday's 128-97 victory over the Memphis Grizzlies .

He shot 14-of-20 from the field, including 4-of-7 from beyond the arc, while adding five assists.

The performance followed consecutive 20-point outings against the Cleveland Cavaliers.

Mitchell scored 20 points on Nov. 2 before producing 23 points and seven rebounds two days later.

His offensive development has been particularly valuable with several established Thunder players sidelined.

Now, Oklahoma City must replace his production while navigating an increasingly depleted rotation.

Thunder Face Growing Injury Crisis Against Trail Blazers

Mitchell joins a lengthy list of unavailable players.

Chet Holmgren remains out because of right knee injury recovery, while Jalen Williams is sidelined following left ankle surgery.

Cason Wallace is also out after undergoing left shoulder surgery.

Meanwhile, Jaylin Williams will miss another game because of lower back spasms.

Thomas Sorber is recovering from right knee surgery, and Nikola Topic remains unavailable while on a G League assignment.

Those absences place additional pressure on Gilgeous-Alexander.

The reigning NBA Most Valuable Player scored 26 points against Portland on Tuesday but struggled with his efficiency.

Gilgeous-Alexander shot 8-of-22 from the field and missed all four of his 3-point attempts.

He also grabbed eight rebounds but sat out the fourth quarter as Portland pulled away.

Jared McCain provided one of Oklahoma City's few offensive bright spots, finishing with 21 points.

With Mitchell unavailable, McCain could take on an expanded scoring role Wednesday.

Veteran guard Alex Caruso and rookie Bennett Stirtz could also receive additional opportunities in Daigneault's rotation.

Recently acquired Nique Clifford is another option after making his Thunder debut Tuesday.

Clifford, acquired from Sacramento for future second-round draft picks, scored four points in nearly 20 minutes.

The Thunder will need more contributions from their available guards against a Portland team coming off a convincing victory.

Damian Lillard led the Trail Blazers with 25 points Tuesday, while Deni Avdija added 24 points and eight assists.

Portland improved to 7-3 with the victory.

For Oklahoma City, Wednesday's rematch offers an immediate chance to respond.

But without Mitchell and several other rotation regulars, the Thunder face an increasingly difficult task.

Ahead of the 2012-13 season, the Charlotte Bobcats acquired Ben Gordon and a first-round pick from Detroit in exchange for Corey Maggette. Gordon, a former 21-point-per-game scorer, was entering his ninth NBA season after stints with the Bulls and Pistons. In his first year with the Bobcats, Gordon played 75 games, averaging 11.2 points, 1.7 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 0.5 steals in 20.8 minutes. Unfortunately for Gordon, his second year in Charlotte didn't go as planned, as he was waived after 19 games averaging 5.2 points.

Gordon, a UConn alum, would go on to play one final season with the Orlando Magic (2014-15) before finishing his NBA career after 11 seasons. He ended his career with 744 appearances and averaged 14.9 points, 2.5 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 0.7 steals. articles.title: How Celtics’ Paul George spoiling Jaylen Brown’s revenge game is a big win for Brad Stevens
articles.summary: Boston Celtics veteran Paul George drew first blood against his former team, scoring a season-high 36 points in a 123-101 blowout win over the Philadelphia...
articles.body:
Boston Celtics veteran Paul George drew first blood against his former team, scoring a season-high 36 points in a 123-101 blowout win over the Philadelphia 76ers, who traded with Brad Stevens for Jaylen Brown this summer. It was the biggest storyline in the NBA. Amid the hoopla around the Celtics' Jayson Tatum and 76ers' Brown squaring off for the first time, George reminded fans of the player sent to Boston in exchange for Jaylen.

The veteran that Celtics president of basketball operations Brad Stevens saw as a better fit for his team, on the court and on his spreadsheet. George was part of one of the most shocking trades in recent NBA history, as the Celtics split their star tandem after nearly a decade of one of the franchise's most successful eras.

In nine years, Tatum and Brown led the Celtics to five Eastern Conference Finals appearances, two NBA Finals berths, and, most importantly, a 2024 championship that ended a 16-year drought. After failing to make a deep playoff run in back-to-back years, including a first-round exit against the 76ers, Stevens pulled the trigger on trading Brown for George and a package of draft picks during the offseason.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The NBA world and Celtics fans alike quickly pointed to the dynamic of Tatum and Brown's relationship as a contributing factor. Despite Brown coming off the best season of his career, and doing it without Tatum, Stevens saw it as the ideal time to part ways, especially after another failed run to return to the NBA Finals, where Boston hasn't come close to reaching since its last title.

Financially, the move made sense for the Celtics' bottom line, as George entered the third year of a four-year, $211.5 million contract, worth $54.1 million, with a player option for the 2027-28 season. Brown, meanwhile, is in the third year of a five-year, $285.3 million contract with no option attached to the backend, and the deal won't expire until 2029.

George undoubtedly gives the Celtics optionality without the restrictions that come with two players taking up 70 percent of the cap. However, that same optionality applies to what the Celtics get on the basketball court. That's where George went 14-for-22, including six threes against his former team Tuesday night. He also finished with five rebounds and one assist as Boston cruised to its ninth regular-season win.

While most envisioned Celtics veterans such as Derrick White and Payton Pritchard filling the void left by Brown's absence offensively, George has taken matters into his own hands so far. He's averaging 22.0 points on impressive 48.8/44.0/82.1 shooting splits, 5.2 rebounds, 3.8 assists, and 2.1 steals per game. Paul's career has been rejuvenated since his trade to the Celtics.

With a clean slate of health, George reminded fans of the injury setbacks that plagued his two seasons with the 76ers and how what we're seeing in the early stages of the regular season is a byproduct of his health.

"That was the biggest challenge, the biggest hurdle my first two years I was here in Philly. And then what I've learned is I'm a little bit better with more usage," George said. "And that's no knock to how my opportunities here with Philly. Quite frankly, I wasn't healthy to take on the workload that I feel I'm at my best at. Here in Boston, they gave me an opportunity to come out here, play, and be myself. Joe [Mazzulla] has integrated me right into the offense and allowed me to just be myself."

Celtics president of basketball operations Brad Stevens was forced to delete his Instagram account after his trade for Paul George. That's how bad the comments and messages from Celtics fans got, frustrated at watching their team trade away Brown for an aging George. But Boston's early success is what Stevens envisioned for the long term of the 2026-27 season.

George has only missed one game for the Celtics so far. Boston improved to 9-2, sitting atop the Eastern Conference standings and second-best in the NBA.

Is Paul George a better fit for Jayson Tatum, Celtics?

It's still early in the 2026-27 season. However, that didn't stop one analyst from saying Paul George's fit with the Celtics is better than Jaylen Brown's. George alongside Tatum beats the eye test compared to Brown, and it's showing in the box score and, of course, in the Eastern Conference standings for a Celtics team that now has the best record, as Yahoo Sports' Kevin O'Connor noted after Tuesday's win.

"Paul George is a better fit next to Jayson Tatum than Jaylen Brown ever was. I know, it's soon. I know Tatum and Brown won a Finals together. But I feel the synergy between these two guys early this season, with Paul George averaging 20 on elite efficiency, elite three-point volume, the connective passing from him as well, and the ability to be an initiator," said O'Connor on his podcast.

"It just feels like these two guys, they just gel. It feels natural to me. So even if George isn't as great in a vacuum as Jaylen Brown is, I feel like this is a better fit. These guys actually fit."

The Celtics will face the Raptors on the second night of a back-to-back on Wednesday.
